meetings.title: City Council Work Session on the Budget June 4, 2026
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council held its third budget work session on June 4, 2026, to reach consensus on final fiscal adjustments prior to budget adoption. Council members negotiated compromises on fund balance usage ($650k), reductions to the homeless strategic framework via ARPA interest ($650k), and funding restorations for immigrant legal defense, basic income, and outside agencies. Staff was directed to finalize the reconciled budget package ahead of the formal adoption vote scheduled for June 15, 2026.

agenda_items.title: Opening Remarks and Budget Work Session Overview
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager and Budget Director Christina Riordan introduced the third budget work session for fiscal year 2026-2027, highlighting that this session serves as an informal working meeting to finalize major budget reconciliation items before formal adoption. Council members discussed overall fiscal constraints, revenue limitations, and the overarching goal of balancing the budget without increasing property taxes.

agenda_items.title: Landscape and Consensus Framework Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tem reviewed consensus points gathered from one-on-one meetings with council members, including partially restoring funding for non-profits, increasing immigrant legal defense funding, parking pilots, crossing guards, and closing basic income gaps. Council members debated various revenue sources, including ARPA interest and neighborhood revitalization grants.

agenda_items.title: Worker Pay, Bonuses, and Property Tax Rate Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council debated worker compensation, keeping employee pay increases at 2%, and Council Member Baker's proposal for a quarter-penny property tax increase to fund worker bonuses. Other members strongly opposed property tax increases due to burdens on seniors and fixed-income residents.

agenda_items.title: General Fund Fund Balance and Financial Reserves Analysis
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Finance Director Tim Flohr and Budget Director Christina Riordan presented details on the general fund fund balance, explaining the 16.7% policy minimum versus historical practice and surplus levels (approximately $5M above target). Council members discussed the pros and cons of dipping into fund balance for one-time capital and program needs versus maintaining financial reserves for economic uncertainty.

agenda_items.title: Community Safety Fleet Needs and Operational Efficiency
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager and staff addressed vehicle and fleet needs for the Community Safety Department (HART program) and Welcome Home program. Council members discussed whether to fund fleet purchases or explore leasing/financing options amidst tight budget constraints.

agenda_items.title: Housing Stability, Eviction Diversion, and Homeless Strategic Framework
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council members reviewed housing and rental support funding, comparing city allocations with county contributions through DSS (Department of Social Services) for eviction diversion and homelessness strategic framework initiatives.

agenda_items.title: Final Consensus Building and Budget Reconciliation Direction
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council arrived at a tentative consensus framework involving a blend of funding adjustments: $650k from fund balance, $650k from ARPA interest (scaling back the homeless strategic framework slightly), $300k from neighborhood revitalization grants, and partial restoration for non-profit and community partners, aiming to finalize the budget by June 15.

disagreements.meeting_title: City Council Work Session on the Budget June 4, 2026
disagreements.issue: Property Tax Increase for Worker Bonuses vs. Tax Stability
disagreements.summary: Council Member Baker proposed a 0.25-penny property tax increase to fund employee bonuses, while other members strongly opposed raising property taxes due to impacts on seniors and fixed-income residents.
disagreements.side_a_position: Support a quarter-penny tax increase to fund worker bonuses.
side_a_arguments: Workers face tight budget constraints and employee pay was restricted; incremental tax increases are sustainable.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose any property tax increase.
side_b_arguments: Tax increases heavily burden seniors and residents on fixed incomes during uncertain economic times.
disagreements.resolution: Rejected; council reached consensus not to raise property taxes, keeping rates flat.

disagreements.meeting_title: City Council Work Session on the Budget June 4, 2026
disagreements.issue: Fund Balance Drawdown vs. Fiscal Reserve Caution
disagreements.summary: Debate over whether to draw down fund balance below target levels to finance one-time community requests, ultimately resolved via a $650k compromise combined with matching reductions in the homeless strategic framework.
disagreements.side_a_position: Open to utilizing fund balance (up to $1M) to avoid cutting essential community programs.
side_a_arguments: This is an extraordinary budget year, and fund balance exists precisely as a reserve for exceptional needs.
disagreements.side_b_position: Strictly limit or oppose fund balance drawdown.
side_b_arguments: Economic uncertainty and potential state legislative caps require maintaining financial flexibility and high credit ratings.
disagreements.resolution: Resolved via compromise to draw $650k from fund balance combined with a $650k reduction in the homeless strategic framework (ARPA interest) and reducing ADA allotment to half.

meetings.title: Durham Joint City County Planning Committee (JCCPC) - June 3, 2026
meetings.executive_summary: Convening without functioning room monitors on June 3, 2026, Chair Nate Baker and JCCPC members unanimously approved the May 4 minutes before diving into two contentious policy items. First, Baker objected to softening Comprehensive Plan policy language produced by the EAR ad hoc subcommittee ('should' to 'encourage and incentivize'), sparking pushback from Matt Kopac, Javiera Caballero, and Wendy Jacobs before a same-meeting compromise allowed the EAR policies to advance via informal consensus. Second, members scrutinized a staff-initiated amendment deleting UDO Section 3.19.6.B onward—removing local 60-day/12-month moratorium caps and Planning Commission hearings—with County members warning of RTP economic uncertainty and Shanetta Burris questioning indefinite extensions, while Council members stressed the urgent July 3 expiration of the 60-day data center moratorium.

agenda_items.title: Roll Call, Agenda Reordering, and Approval of May 4, 2026 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Despite audio/video monitor failures requiring paper packets, Chair Nate Baker called roll with Javiera Caballero, Matt Kopac, Shanetta Burris, Planning Commission Chair Chagaris, and County Commissioner Wendy Jacobs present (Stephen Valentine joined ~15 minutes later). The committee reordered the agenda to consider Items 7 and 8 ahead of Items 5 and 6 and unanimously approved the May 4, 2026 minutes.

agenda_items.title: EAR Comprehensive Plan Policy and Commentary Edits
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Aaron Cain presented final Evaluation and Assessment Report (EAR) policy and commentary revisions drafted by the four-member ad hoc subcommittee (Burris, Kopac, Jacobs, Valentine) to prevent developers from 'double-dipping' points. Debate erupted over Javiera Caballero's request for a policy prioritization framework and Nate Baker's objection to softer verbs in Policies 40, 48, 101, 172, and 177; after revisiting the item at 01:00:30, members compromised on most edits (retaining Baker's noted dissent on Policy 40) and gave thumbs-up to advance the package.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Informational with informal thumbs-up consensus after compromise

agenda_items.title: UDO Section 3.19.6 Moratorium Text Amendment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Robin Schultz and Sara Young presented a staff-initiated amendment deleting Section 3.19.6.B onward to eliminate local 60-day initial limits, 12-month maximum caps, and Planning Commission public hearings on development moratoria, leaving only NCGS 160D-107 rules. County Commissioners Wendy Jacobs and Stephen Valentine flagged business uncertainty and removing Planning Commission oversight, Shanetta Burris questioned extensions past 12 months citing Tahoe-Sierra, and Baker, Caballero, and Kopac emphasized meeting the June 15 Council deadline before the July 3 data center moratorium sunset.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Informational / Scheduled for June 9 Planning Commission, June 15 Council, June 22 BOCC

agenda_items.title: Destination 2055 Metropolitan Transportation Plan (MTP)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Doug Plachcinski and Colleen McGuinness of Triangle West TPO presented the $34+ billion fiscally constrained 30-year Destination 2055 MTP ($8B transit, $9B roadway O&M, $13B multimodal street upgrades, $4.2B bike/ped), noting reliance on a 2035 county sales-tax expansion, opposition to a $500M US-70 conversion segment, and closure of the Durham-Roxboro rail trail corridor.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Case Preview (Highlands & Cheek Road)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Javar Jones previewed two cases inside the UGB: Highlands (Baptist Rd/Santee Rd, 88.44 acres, RR to PDR 3.618 for up to 320 residential units with 5% at 80% AMI for 30 years via non-contiguous annexation) and 3513 & 3515 Cheek Road (3.99 acres, RS to RSMD textual for up to 40 townhouses via satellite annexation).

agenda_items.title: FY26 Work Program Community Planning Projects
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Scott Whiteman gave a brief status update on ongoing FY26 Community Planning projects, noting the multimodal TIA timeline shifted toward August and fall adoption, before Chair Baker adjourned the meeting at 11:36 a.m.

votes.item_title: Approval of May 4, 2026 JCCPC Minutes
votes.notes: Joint City-County Planning Committee voice vote; Planning Commission Chair Chagaris and County Commissioner Wendy Jacobs also present and voting Aye (County Commissioner Stephen Valentine arrived later at 00:20:32).
votes.discussion_detail: Opening the June 3, 2026 JCCPC session despite malfunctioning room display monitors, Chair Nate Baker completed roll call—with City Council members Baker, Javiera Caballero, Matt Kopac, and Shanetta Burris alongside Planning Commission Chair Chagaris and County Commissioner Wendy Jacobs present—and reordered the agenda to prioritize EAR policies and moratorium text amendments. Baker then asked for approval of the May 4, 2026 meeting minutes. No edits or objections were raised by members. Following a motion and second, the minutes passed unanimously by voice vote.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham Joint City County Planning Committee (JCCPC) - June 3, 2026
disagreements.issue: EAR Comprehensive Plan Policy Language Softening and Subcommittee Process
disagreements.summary: Committee members sparred over whether edits from the four-member EAR ad hoc subcommittee improperly weakened mandatory policy directives and whether JCCPC should delay action to August or create a policy-weighting framework.
disagreements.side_a_position: Object to weakening directive verbs ('should') in key Comp Plan policies and seek a pause or policy-prioritization framework to curb selective developer compliance.
side_a_arguments: Nate Baker objected to replacing 'should' with 'encourage and incentivize' in Policy 40 and similar softening in Policies 48, 101, 172 ('price points' to 'sizes'), and 177 ('incorporate' to 'allow for'), initially requesting postponement to August.

Javiera Caballero criticized wealthy applicants gaming competing natural-heritage and 20% affordable-housing policies and pushed for a future policy prioritization hierarchy (briefly clashing with Wendy Jacobs over staff bandwidth).
disagreements.side_b_position: Respect the 10-month bipartisan/joint subcommittee consensus without further delay or overloading staff ahead of data-center and LDC deadlines.
side_b_arguments: Matt Kopac and Javiera Caballero warned against delaying 10 months of subcommittee work on the EAR package until August.
County Commissioner Wendy Jacobs pushed back against adding a new policy-ranking project given already stretched staff capacity for data center rules and LDC drafting.
disagreements.resolution: Resolved later in the same meeting ([01:00:56]-[01:12:11]): Baker dropped objections to Policies 48, 101, and 172, accepted 'encourage' in Policy 177, and placed his disagreement on Policy 40 on the record as JCCPC gave thumbs-up consensus to forward the EAR package.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham Joint City County Planning Committee (JCCPC) - June 3, 2026
disagreements.issue: Repealing UDO Section 3.19.6 Moratorium Caps and Planning Commission Hearing Requirement
disagreements.summary: Members debated staff's proposal to repeal all local moratorium restrictions in UDO Section 3.19.6 beyond subsection A—eliminating the 60-day initial cap, 12-month total cap, and Planning Commission public hearing—to rely solely on state statute NCGS 160D-107.
disagreements.side_a_position: Urgently enable moratorium extensions past 60 days/12 months before the July 3 data center moratorium expires.
side_a_arguments: Nate Baker, Javiera Caballero, and Matt Kopac emphasized that City Council needed to adopt the UDO amendment on June 15 so the 60-day data center moratorium would not lapse on July 3 while permanent regulations are drafted.
disagreements.side_b_position: Question removing Planning Commission public hearings for all future moratoria and exceeding 12-month caps without legal and RTP economic guardrails.
side_b_arguments: County Commissioners Wendy Jacobs and Stephen Valentine warned that eliminating Planning Commission public input and removing local caps creates legal exposure and chills business investment in RTP and Treyburn.
Shanetta Burris questioned the legal justification for extending development moratoria past 12 months, citing heightened constitutional scrutiny under Tahoe-Sierra.
disagreements.resolution: No JCCPC vote taken; text amendment proceeded to Planning Commission (June 9), City Council (June 15), and BOCC (June 22) with committee concerns entered into the record.

meetings.title: Second Public Hearing on the Proposed Budget 2026-27 June 1, 2026
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council held its second public hearing on the proposed 2026-27 budget and capital improvement plan. The meeting consisted entirely of public comments regarding budget priorities, including funding for eviction diversion, immigration legal services, the DEAR expunction program, youth violence intervention (Grace Inc.), park environmental lead remediation, and city worker compensation, with final budget adoption scheduled for June 15, 2026.

agenda_items.title: FY 2026-27 Proposed Budget and CIP Staff Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Christina Reen, Director of Budget and Management Services, presented the second public hearing on the proposed fiscal year 2026-27 budget and 2027-32 capital improvement plan. She noted that the proposed property tax rate remains unchanged at 43.71 cents per $100 of assessed value, and outlined the schedule leading to final budget adoption on June 15th.

agenda_items.title: Opening of Second Public Hearing on Proposed Budget
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Leonardo Williams officially declared open the second public hearing on the proposed fiscal year 2026-27 budget, establishing ground rules for public speakers and outlining the process for hearing community input.

agenda_items.title: Public Comments on Eviction Diversion, Legal Aid, and Housing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Numerous residents and legal aid advocates spoke regarding the proposed funding for eviction diversion programs and legal services. Landlords raised concerns about judicial delays affecting housing supply, while tenants and legal aid advocates emphasized the vital role of legal representation in preventing homelessness.

agenda_items.title: Public Comments on Youth Violence Intervention & Community Safety
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Community members and representatives from youth organizations and violence intervention programs advocated for stable, ongoing funding for proactive violence prevention and community safety initiatives.

agenda_items.title: Public Comments on Environmental Justice and Park Contamination
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Speakers addressed environmental justice concerns, calling for dedicated funding to clean up contaminated historical parks in minority neighborhoods and expressing concerns over transit route equity.

agenda_items.title: Public Comments on City Worker Pay, Step Plans, and Compensation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Union representatives and city workers addressed the council regarding inflation, cost of living pressures, and the importance of maintaining worker step plans, merit raises, and fair compensation.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Meeting June 1, 2026
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council held a regular meeting and public budget hearing on June 1, 2026, to discuss the proposed FY 2026-27 budget, capital improvement plan, board appointments, and service contracts. The council approved the consent agenda, board appointments, the Durham Strategic Framework to Prevent and End Homelessness, and a 5-year Municipal Service District contract with Downtown Durham Inc. After extensive public comment on housing, eviction diversion, environmental justice, worker pay, and community safety, the council approved a $16+ million contract renewal and expansion with Axon Enterprises for police technology and body cameras by a 6-1 vote, alongside holding the second public hearing on the city manager's proposed budget.

agenda_items.title: Meeting Opening and Council Member Comments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Meeting called to order by Mayor Williams, followed by moment of silence and Pledge of Allegiance. Council members shared announcements and reflections on Pride Month, Juneteenth flag raising, community events, and the upcoming budget challenges.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda and Board Appointments (Items 1-9)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager, City Attorney, and City Clerk presented priority items. The consent agenda and board/commission appointments (Items 5 and 9) were reviewed and voted upon, while items 10, 11, 29, and 30 were pulled for individual discussion.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed, 7-0 (Consent Agenda and Items 5 & 9 approved separately)

agenda_items.title: Amendment to FY 2025-26 Budget and Capital Project Ordinances
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public speakers and council discussed budget adjustments and community allocations. Council moved to approve amendments to the FY 2025-26 budget and capital project ordinances.

agenda_items.title: Adoption of Durham Strategic Framework to Prevent and End Homelessness
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public speakers commented on housing stability, homelessness strategies, and interim site needs. Council discussed and adopted the Durham Strategic Framework to Prevent and End Homelessness.

agenda_items.title: One-Hour Free Parking Program Proposal
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public speaker proposed expanding free parking options in downtown municipal decks to support local small businesses. Council discussed the one-hour free parking proposal.

agenda_items.title: Downtown Durham Municipal Service District Operations Contract with Downtown Durham Inc.
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public hearing held for the Downtown Durham Municipal Service District operations contract. Following staff reports and public comments (with Council Member Burris recusing himself as a DDI board member), council authorized the 5-year contract with Downtown Durham Inc.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed, 6-0 (1 abstention by Council Member Burris)

agenda_items.title: Axon Enterprise Inc. Contract Renewal and Expansion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Extensive public comment and council deliberation regarding the renewal and expansion of the Axon Enterprise contract (~$16M) including body cameras, data management, drones, and Fusus platform integration. Concerns were raised regarding surveillance, privacy, and international tech ties, while police leadership and supporters emphasized violent crime realities and evidence management.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing on Proposed FY 2026-27 Budget & CIP
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented an overview of the proposed FY 2026-27 budget and Capital Improvement Plan (CIP). Public comments spanned numerous community concerns including eviction diversion funding, immigration legal services, community center leases, park environmental remediation, and city worker/firefighter merit raises.

votes.item_title: Audit Services Oversight Committee Appointments (Item 5)
votes.notes: Nominated Nicholas W. Long and Maisha Akal Tree Morris
votes.discussion_detail: The council unanimously approved (7-0) the appointments of Nicholas W. Long and Maisha Akal Tree Morris to the Audit Services Oversight Committee. The nominations were presented by staff as part of the board and committee appointment process preceding the general business agenda.

votes.item_title: Mayor's Council for Women Appointments (Item 9)
votes.notes: Appointed Stephanie Williams, Sheena Matthews, Sarah Stanfield, and Tiffany R. Foster
votes.discussion_detail: The council unanimously approved (7-0) appointments to the Mayor's Council for Women after resolving remaining vacancies and at-large voting tallies. Council members nominated Stephanie Williams for the Cultural, Recreation, and Fine Arts Sector, Sheena Matthews for Fair Housing and Economic Development, Sarah Stanfield for Ward Three, and Tiffany R. Foster for the at-large seat following a tally adjustment.

votes.item_title: Amendment to FY 2025-26 Budget and Capital Project Ordinances (Item 10)
votes.notes: Pulled and approved
votes.discussion_detail: The council considered and unanimously adopted (7-0) the amendment to the FY 2025-26 budget and capital project ordinances. Prior to the vote, public commenters raised significant concerns regarding funding cuts to community programs, the termination of the Durham Parks and Rec contract with the West End Community Foundation, and the need to support violence interrupter programs. Council members acknowledged the heavy public feedback and competing budget priorities before moving forward with the ordinance amendments as recommended by the city attorney.

votes.item_title: Adoption of Durham Strategic Framework to Prevent and End Homelessness (Item 11)
votes.notes: Approved resolution
votes.discussion_detail: The council unanimously adopted (7-0) the resolution approving the Durham Strategic Framework to Prevent and End Homelessness, involving a proposed $13 million strategy. Public speakers expressed strong concerns that the framework heavily subsidizes private landlords while failing to address interim measures such as police sweeps of homeless encampments or providing community-led safe sleeping and parking sites. Despite criticisms regarding the allocation toward housing subsidies and the lack of explicit protections against sweeps, the council moved forward and passed the strategic framework unanimously.

votes.item_title: Downtown Durham Municipal Service District Operations Contract with Downtown Durham Inc. (Item 35)
votes.notes: 5-year contract ($1,948,495 for FY 2026-27); Council Member Burris recused due to DDI board membership
votes.discussion_detail: The City Council considered authorizing a five-year contract with Downtown Durham Incorporated (DDI) to operate the Downtown Durham Municipal Service District from July 1, 2026, through June 30, 2031, with a fiscal year 2026-27 amount not to exceed $1,948,495, subject to budget authorization. Public input and council discussions addressed topics such as living wage commitments, increased resident representation in decision-making, and questions around privatizing core government services rather than utilizing city employees. Council Member Burris formally recused himself from the vote upon the city attorney's advisement due to his position as a DDI board member. Other council members praised the DDI ambassador program for uplifting downtown hospitality and supporting small businesses. Ultimately, the motion passed unanimously with one abstention (6-0).

votes.item_title: Axon Enterprise Inc. Contract Renewal and Expansion (Item 26)
votes.notes: Contract amount not to exceed $16,099,402.28
votes.discussion_detail: The City Council debated and voted on authorizing a contract renewal and expansion with Axon Enterprise Inc. in an amount not to exceed $16,099,402.28. Public speakers strongly urged opposition to the contract, citing concerns over the addition of surveillance drones, the Fusus platform, data storage, and potential AI-driven predictive policing. Council discussion weighed the constitutional rights and safety of residents against escalating violent crime statistics, with the Mayor highlighting dramatic increases in shootings and direct feedback from residents demanding more security cameras and police presence. While some council members explored delaying the vote for two weeks to consult with the ACLU and review CCOPS model ordinances, the motion moved forward. Ultimately, the contract renewal and expansion passed by a 6-1 vote, with Council Member Baker casting the sole dissenting vote.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham City Council Meeting June 1, 2026
disagreements.issue: Renewal and expansion of the Axon police technology, surveillance, and body camera contract (Item 26) totaling ~$16 million.
disagreements.summary: Debate over whether to approve a $16+ million contract renewal and expansion with Axon for police body cameras, drones, and digital evidence management amid community pushback against surveillance technologies.
disagreements.side_a_position: Support for renewing and expanding the Axon contract with proper guardrails.
side_a_arguments: Violent crime and heavy weaponry on the streets require robust law enforcement tools; contract provides necessary body-worn cameras, efficient digital evidence management for the DA's office, and secure city-controlled data encryption.
disagreements.side_b_position: Opposition to expanding police surveillance technology and request to reallocate funds to community needs.
side_b_arguments: Surveillance technology, drones, license plate readers, and Fusus real-time crime platforms threaten privacy, risk misuse, and divert millions of dollars away from root-cause community investments like affordable housing, youth programs, and mental health.
disagreements.resolution: Passed 6-1, with Council Member Baker voting nay.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session on the Budget May 28, 2026
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council held its second day of budget work session retreats for the FY 2027 budget on May 28, 2026. The council received detailed departmental presentations from the Transportation Department (highlighting transit awards, fare-free operations through FY 2027, and impending structural deficits in FY 2028), the Community Safety Department (covering homelessness strategic framework, HEART, and program reductions), and the Office of Economic and Workforce Development (covering YouthWorks, small business support, and economic mobility). Additionally, the council reviewed Capital Improvement Program (CIP) options regarding athletic court repairs, ultimately reaching consensus to maintain $3 million in FY 2027 with future-year commitments.

agenda_items.title: Transportation Department Budget Presentation & Transit Fund Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Transportation Director Sean Egan presented GoDurham transit accomplishments, awards, and significant fiscal challenges (projected $3.3M FY26 deficit, balanced FY27 via one-time county assistance, and $13.8M FY28 structural deficit). Council discussed fare-free transit, safety, and transit fund sustainability.

agenda_items.title: Community Safety Department Budget Presentation & Homeless Strategic Framework
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Community Safety Director Ryan Smith presented the proposed budget for the Community Safety Department (HEART, Office of Survivor Care, Welcome Home, and Involuntary Response Team) and the $4.5M city contribution to the Homeless Strategic Framework. Council debated homeless coordination, funding commitments from county/philanthropic partners, eviction diversion, and guaranteed income cuts.

agenda_items.title: Office of Economic and Workforce Development (OEWD) Budget Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: OEWD Director presented budget updates, small business support, Youth Works expansion, worker cooperative initiatives, and economic mobility strategies. Council discussed youth financial literacy, bank account access, and historic corridor investments.

agenda_items.title: Traffic Calming & Speed Hump Program Reduction
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager presented a minor budget reduction pausing the community-driven speed hump petition program ($20,000 reduction) while transportation staff reevaluate systemic and equitable traffic calming approaches.

agenda_items.title: Capital Improvement Program (CIP) - Athletic Court Repairs & Policy Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented options regarding CIP funding levels for athletic court repairs ($3M proposed vs $8M requested by council members). Council and staff discussed capacity limits, project management, scoping studies, and scoring formulas, agreeing to maintain $3M in FY27 with future scoping.

disagreements.meeting_title: City Council Work Session on the Budget May 28, 2026
disagreements.issue: Funding for the homeless strategic framework and coordination with external/county partners
disagreements.summary: Debate over whether to fully fund the city's portion of the homelessness strategic framework given uncertainty in county and philanthropic matching funds.
disagreements.side_a_position: Skeptical of full upfront funding without firm county/philanthropic commitments
side_a_arguments: Council members expressed concern about committing significant city funds upfront without guaranteed partner buy-in, questioning whether the city is taking on disproportionate social services burdens compared to the county.
side_a_members: Mayor Pro Tem Caballero, Mayor Williams
disagreements.side_b_position: Supportive of funding the framework to catalyze wider investment
side_b_arguments: Staff and other council members emphasized that the city must show leadership and commitment first to unlock private and county funding, and that immediate action is necessary to address homelessness drivers.
side_b_members: Director Ryan Smith, Council Member Burris
disagreements.resolution: Maintained city's proposed share ($4.5M) while noting concerns over whether county and philanthropic partners will fully meet their commitments, affecting year-one reduction targets.

disagreements.meeting_title: City Council Work Session on the Budget May 28, 2026
disagreements.issue: Capital Improvement Program (CIP) funding levels for athletic court repairs
disagreements.summary: Discussion on whether to increase immediate CIP funding for athletic courts versus staff capacity limits and trade-offs with other infrastructure projects.
disagreements.side_a_position: Increase immediate CIP allocation for athletic courts
side_a_arguments: Advocated for increasing athletic court funding immediately to $4-8 million over two years to address severe deterioration and safety hazards.
disagreements.side_b_position: Maintain proposed $3M cap with out-year prioritization
side_b_arguments: Staff noted contracting and capacity limitations (max delivery around $3-4M/year) and cautioned against trading off essential infrastructure like curb ramps and sidewalk repairs or trail projects.
side_b_members: City Manager, Budget Director, City Staff
disagreements.resolution: Reached consensus to stick with the manager's proposed $3 million for FY 2027 (plus available carryover balance) while planning for additional out-year investments rather than cutting other infrastructure like curb ramps or trails.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session on the Budget May 27, 2026
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council held a work session on May 27, 2026, to discuss the proposed FY27 budget, focusing on fiscal context, property tax assessments, revenue streams, staff pay and benefits, and capital improvement projects. Staff presented an unusual budget environment characterized by a $3 billion decline in assessed property tax base due to over 10,000 successful property revaluation appeals (particularly from commercial office buildings and apartments), slowing sales tax growth, and rising personnel/operating costs. To balance the budget with no property tax rate increase (maintaining 43.71 cents per $100), the city utilized department reductions, outside agency cuts, vacancy rate savings, and the elimination of pay-for-performance merit increases in favor of a 2% structure adjustment and funding for the $25.09/hr minimum livable wage. No formal votes or roll-call motions were recorded during this work session, as it was strictly an informational and deliberative workshop.

agenda_items.title: FY27 Budget Overview and General Fund Revenue Outlook
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Director Christina Riordan presented the FY27 proposed budget overview, highlighting an unusual budget environment shaped by property tax assessment appeals, slowing sales tax growth, rising personnel and operating costs, and inflation. The city manager and budget team discussed strategies for balancing the budget without a tax increase, including departmental reductions and eliminating pay-for-performance in favor of a 2% structure adjustment. Council members engaged in extensive deliberation regarding vacancy rates, departmental cuts, and the overall tax rate compared to peer cities.

agenda_items.title: Durham County Property Tax Revaluation and Appeals Process
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Durham County Tax Administrator Mr. Doyle presented detailed findings regarding the unprecedented surge of over 10,500 property tax appeals following the county-wide revaluation. Discussion focused on the distinction between residential and commercial appeals, the impact of commercial office and apartment vacancies, and the challenges of projecting holdbacks when appeal deadlines extend past initial budgeting dates. Council members raised questions about data timeliness, the Board of Equalization and Review (BOER), and potential legal or structural reforms.

agenda_items.title: FY27 Employee Pay, Compensation Plans, and Benefits Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Human Resources presented the proposed pay and benefits package for FY27, including the implementation of the Durham Minimum Livable Wage (DMLW) at $25.09/hour and a 2% across-the-board structure adjustment. Staff reviewed pay plans, historical wage growth, employee tenure examples, and the upcoming classification and compensation study. Council members discussed salary compression, minimum livable wage calculations for firefighters working 24-hour shifts, and comparison with private sector benefits.

agenda_items.title: 10-Year Capital Improvement Program (CIP) Model and Project Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented the 10-year Capital Improvement Program (CIP) model and proposed project appropriations. Discussion centered around funding allocations for athletic courts (tennis and basketball courts), sidewalk and street paving, internal facilities like the Environmental Street Services building, and project prioritization scoring. Council members debated trade-offs between internal keep-the-lights-on projects and community-facing infrastructure needs, setting homework to review project lists and priorities for the following day's session.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Work Session May 21, 2026
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council held a work session on May 21, 2026, discussing several key policy and budgetary issues. Major items included a comprehensive presentation and debate on a proposed multi-year technology contract bundle with Axon for police body-worn cameras, tasers, and vehicle cameras; a briefing and discussion on municipal election timing, ward representation, and plurality voting; and an environmental update regarding severe industrial contamination by Brenntag and city/state regulatory enforcement. The council also addressed public comments concerning unhoused encampments, affordable housing and legal aid, police funding, and community safety.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review and Adjustments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The council and city officials reviewed the meeting agenda, noting priority items, supplementary additions, and items pulled by council members for separate discussion and debate.

agenda_items.title: Overview of Durham Municipal Elections & Charter Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The council held a comprehensive discussion and debate on Durham municipal elections overview, examining potential charter changes including moving to even-year elections, four-year mayoral terms, true ward representation, and plurality voting vs. primaries.

agenda_items.title: Motion to Enter Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Attorney presented a motion to hold a closed session pursuant to NCGS 143-318.11(a)(3) for attorney-client consultation regarding pending litigation including Isaac Woods Jr. v. City of Durham, Cincinnati Insurance Company v. Lisa Mae Cranford et al., and anticipated enforcement actions. The council entertained and approved the motion.

agenda_items.title: Board and Committee Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Clerk presented board and committee appointments for various city-county boards, commissions, and advisory committees, reaching consensus on most nominees while referring undecided appointments to Group Business Agenda (GBA).

agenda_items.title: FY 2025-26 Budget and Capital Project Ordinance Amendments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented requests to amend the fiscal year 2025-2026 budget and associated capital project ordinances to adjust city funding allocations.

agenda_items.title: Durham Strategic Framework to Make Homelessness Rare and Brief by 2031
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented a resolution adopting the Durham Strategic Framework aimed at making homelessness rare and brief by 2031, detailing strategic goals, housing interventions, and coordinated community efforts.

agenda_items.title: Third Amendment to External Auditor Contract
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The council reviewed the third amendment to the external auditor contract to ensure compliance and continued financial oversight services.

agenda_items.title: Cooperative Contracts for Sewer and Stormwater Vacuum Trucks
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented cooperative contracts for purchasing sewer vacuum trucks and stormwater vacuum trucks to support public works infrastructure maintenance.

agenda_items.title: Comprehensive Facilities Condition Assessment Contract
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The council reviewed a contract with HDR Architecture for a comprehensive facilities condition assessment across city buildings and municipal structures.

agenda_items.title: Eminent Domain Actions for SW45 Bike and Sidewalk Project Easements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The council discussed eminent domain actions to obtain temporary construction easements along West Cornwallis Road for the SW45 Bike and Sidewalk Project.

agenda_items.title: Park Renovations and Parking Facility Maintenance Contracts
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The council reviewed construction contracts for park renovations at River Forest Park, Old Farm Park, American Village, West Point on the Eno, and parking facility structural maintenance, with several items pulled for separate debate regarding storm recovery and facility maintenance.

agenda_items.title: Economic Development Consulting Contracts
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The council discussed economic development consulting services contracts including the Corridor Bounce Back Program and the Business Registry and Legacy Program (M-Cube and Company and Co Global LLC).

agenda_items.title: Axon Enterprise Inc. Contract Renewal and Expansion Bundle
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The council engaged in extensive debate regarding the Axon enterprise contract bundle for police body-worn cameras, in-car cameras, tasers, drones, and Fusus real-time integration, discussing data privacy, AI tools, surveillance concerns, cost savings, and community safety needs.

agenda_items.title: Trimble Unity Construct Software Contract
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented software licensing, implementation, and managed service support contract for Trimble Unity Construct with Trimble Inc.

agenda_items.title: Woodcroft Parkway Extension Professional Services Contract Amendment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The council discussed amendment number five to the professional services contract with DRMP Inc. for the design of the Woodcroft Parkway extension.

agenda_items.title: One-Hour Free Parking Program Proposal
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented the one-hour free parking program proposal for downtown parking garages (Morgan-Riggbee and Church Street) in partnership with Downtown Durham Incorporated (DDI).

agenda_items.title: Vision Zero 2025 Annual Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The council reviewed the Vision Zero 2025 annual report regarding traffic safety and pedestrian injury reduction initiatives.

agenda_items.title: Water Quality Investigation Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented an informative overview and investigation results regarding city water quality and testing procedures.

agenda_items.title: FY 2025-26 Third Quarter Financial Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The council reviewed the fiscal year 2025-2026 third quarter financial report detailing revenues, expenditures, and budgetary status.

agenda_items.title: FY 2026-27 Proposed Budget and CIP Budget Hearing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The council conducted budget hearings for the city manager's proposed FY 2026-2027 budget and the FY 2027-2032 Capital Improvement Plan (CIP).

agenda_items.title: Economic Development Incentive Agreement with Coco Fro LLC
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The council held a public hearing and reviewed an economic development incentive agreement with Coco Fro LLC.

agenda_items.title: Downtown Durham Municipal Service District Contract
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The council reviewed the FY 2027-2031 contract for Downtown Durham Municipal Service District operations with Downtown Durham Incorporated (DDI).

agenda_items.title: Museum of Durham History Lease Agreement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The council reviewed the lease agreement for the Museum of Durham History located at 521 West Morgan Street.

meetings.title: Durham City Council May 18, 2026
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council met on May 18, 2026, opening with ceremonial proclamations honoring Clinical Trials Day, Huntington's Disease Awareness Month, National Public Works Week, and award-winning transit system GoDurham. The City Manager presented the proposed FY 2026-2027 budget and FY 2027-2032 capital improvement plan. The council debated and unanimously voted down an annexation and utility extension request for 4802 Cheek Road located outside the urban growth boundary (UGB). Finally, the council reviewed and unanimously approved annexation, utility extension, zoning map changes, and a consistency statement for the Sharon Road Assemblage project.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Pledge of Allegiance, and Roll Call
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Leonardo Williams called the meeting to order, followed by a moment of silence and the Pledge of Allegiance led by Council Member Rist. The city clerk conducted the roll call, confirming all council members present.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Proclamations and Recognitions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The mayor and council presented ceremonial proclamations honoring Clinical Trials Day (accepted by Linda Schostek and local medical institution representatives), Huntington's Disease Awareness Month (accepted by Betsy McFarland and Dr. Burton Scott), National Public Works Week (accepted by Director Marvin Williams), and GoDurham Transit System of the Year Award (accepted by Director Sean Egan and transit partners).

agenda_items.title: Council Member and Manager Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council members shared community updates, including congratulations on anniversaries and graduations, upcoming budget public hearings, reflections on national and state legislative issues such as voting rights and right-to-work laws, and community grief over gun violence losses.

agenda_items.title: Manager's Priority Items: Proposed Budget & CIP Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager presented priority items including the proposed Fiscal Year 2026-27 budget and FY 2027-32 Capital Improvement Plan (CIP), highlighting key investments and upcoming budget hearings, as well as an update on the Involuntary Commitment Transportation Plan Agreement.

agenda_items.title: Administrative and Consent Agenda Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The mayor and council reviewed administrative consent items, pulling specific items for separate comment and noting upcoming public hearing dates for the budget.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation and Rezoning for 4802 Cheek Road
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The council held a public hearing on the consolidated annexation and rezoning request for 4802 Cheek Road (Item 21), a proposed residential development outside the Urban Growth Boundary (UGB). Numerous residents and preservation advocates spoke against the project citing UGB violation, environmental and stormwater impacts on Triassic basin soils, lack of infrastructure (fire/EMS), and traffic, while the applicant defended the project's housing and environmental commitments. Following debate, the council voted unanimously to deny the annexation and utility extension.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Failed, 0-7 (Moved/Seconded; unanimous dissenting vote against annexation and utility extension)

agenda_items.title: Biannual Evaluation and Assessment Report (EAR) of Comprehensive Plan
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented the first biannual Evaluation and Assessment Report (EAR) of the Comprehensive Plan, covering proposed Place Type Map changes and UGB adjustments across three separate proposals (Treyburn Corporate Park parcels, a city-acquired lift station site, and a South Alston Avenue parcel). Council discussed the implications of each proposal, public transparency regarding UGB changes, and consistency with comprehensive plan growth policies.

agenda_items.title: Sharon Road Assemblage Annexation, Zoning, and Utility Extension
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The council held a public hearing and deliberation on the Sharon Road Assemblage annexation, utility extension, UDO zoning map change, and consistency statement (Item 23 part / Sharon Road). Residents raised concerns about traffic congestion, safety, and environmental buffers, while the applicant and council discussed increased proffers for affordable housing (8% at 60% AMI plus 2% at 100% AMI) and school contributions ($82,000). The council ultimately approved the annexation, utility extension, zoning change, and consistency statement unanimously.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed, 7-0 (Unanimous approval across annexation/utility extension, UDO zoning map change, and consistency statement)

votes.item_title: Consolidated Annexation 4802 Cheek Road (Item 21)
votes.notes: Failed unanimously following public comments regarding rural preservation, environmental concerns, and infrastructure/emergency service limitations outside the UGB.
votes.discussion_detail: The City Council considered a motion to adopt an ordinance annexing 4802 Cheek Road and to authorize a utility extension agreement with Horizon Land Group LLC. Council members expressed strong opposition, criticizing the proposal as poor planning and highlighting its inconsistency with the comprehensive plan. It was noted that both the planning commission and the county commission spoke forcefully against the project because it is located outside the urban growth boundary (UGB). Council members also raised concerns regarding the negative impacts of large corporate real estate developers on the area. Consequently, the motion failed unanimously in a 0-7 vote.

votes.item_title: Sharon Road Assemblage Annexation & Utility Extension (Item 23)
votes.notes: Passed following developer proffers increasing affordable housing and school contributions.
votes.discussion_detail: The City Council considered a petition from Noel Gosch with Morning Star Law Group for the voluntary annexation and utility extension of two parcels totaling 11.31 acres located at 1921, 2007, and 2013 Sharon Road, developed by Middleburg Development LLC. Discussion focused on negotiated proffers, including increasing income-restricted affordable housing to 8% at 60% AMI and adding 2% at 100% AMI for a 30-year period, as well as raising the Durham Public Schools contribution to $82,000. Council members expressed support for the project's housing strategy and growth within the UGB. The motion to adopt the annexation ordinance and utility extension agreement passed unanimously 7-0.

votes.item_title: Sharon Road Assemblage UDO Zoning Map Change
votes.notes: Passed unanimously.
votes.discussion_detail: The City Council voted to amend the unified development ordinance for the Sharon Road Assemblage, changing the property jurisdiction and zoning from county classifications (industrial light, residential suburban 20, residential rural Falls Jordan Watershed Overlay District B) to city jurisdiction classifications (planned development residential 34.426, commercial general with development plan Falls Jordan Watershed Overlay District B). The motion was moved, seconded, and passed unanimously in a 7-0 vote.

votes.item_title: Sharon Road Assemblage Consistency Statement
votes.notes: Passed unanimously.
votes.discussion_detail: The City Council voted to adopt a consistency statement for the Sharon Road Assemblage zoning map change, as required by North Carolina General Statute Section 160D-605. The motion to confirm consistency was moved, seconded, and passed unanimously in a 7-0 vote.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Work Session May 18, 2026
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council held a meeting on August 24, 2026 (incorporating policy items and public hearings), where they discussed ceremonial items, consent items, and major planning and zoning matters. The council approved several routine items and held a detailed debate on Comprehensive Plan Amendment A25002 regarding evaluation assessment report policy changes, ultimately passing it 4-3 after striking commentary from policy 165. They also addressed zoning map changes and assessment roll confirmations.

agenda_items.title: Council Member Announcements & Community Events
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council members shared announcements and community updates, including highlights from the successful Bimbe Festival run by DPR, the Homegrown Hero Award presented to Kewon Hester, and attendance at the National Adaptation Forum and Bike Month events.

agenda_items.title: City Manager and Department Priority Items Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City management and department heads outlined priority items for the meeting and evening business session, highlighting the FY 2026-27 proposed budget, CIP, proposed water and sewer rates, and the Goose Creek Outfall engineering contract.

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment Period
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Members of the public addressed the council regarding community safety funding, youth mentoring models, Vision Zero land use reforms, and public park and recreation programming support.

agenda_items.title: Review of Administrative Consent & Departmental Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Mayor Pro Tem and City Clerk reviewed administrative consent items, departmental items, presentations, and public hearings scheduled for the evening, pulling specific items for further discussion.

agenda_items.title: FY 2026-27 Proposed Water and Sewer Rates Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Don Greeley from Water Management presented the proposed water and sewer rates for FY 2026-27 and 10-year financial model, highlighting rate objectives, affordability programs, capital improvement spending for Jordan Lake and regulatory compliance, and household bill impacts.

agenda_items.title: City of Durham Involuntary Commitment Transportation Plan Agreement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Community Safety Director Ryan Smith and staff presented the resolution adopting the City of Durham Involuntary Commitment Transportation Plan Agreement, enabling certified first examiners and HART teams to conduct first exams in the community and provide alternative transport. Council members questioned criteria consistency, unmarked vehicle availability, and operational metrics.

agenda_items.title: Coordinated Entry with Diversion Services Contract
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented the contract with Volunteers of America of the Carolinas Inc. for coordinated entry with diversion services. Council discussed why an RFP was not utilized immediately and noted upcoming HUD application schedules and provider capacity.

agenda_items.title: Utility Preliminary Engineering Construction Agreement (Tanaka Pkwy & Red Mill Rd)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff discussed the utility preliminary engineering construction agreement for Tanaka Parkway and Red Mill Road (TIP HE-0007B) involving NCDOT intersection improvements and roundabout installation. Council explored utility relocation cost burdens on local government and coordination with NCDOT.

agenda_items.title: Goose Creek Outfall Project Update & Professional Engineering Contract
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Don Greeley provided an update on the Goose Creek Outfall Project and letter to industry development restrictions, reviewing developer inquiries, outreach meetings, design/construction schedules, and acceleration strategies including early construction packages for interstate bores.

agenda_items.title: Post-Storm Recovery Update (Old Farm & River Forest Neighborhoods)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff from Community Partnerships and Engagement provided a post-storm recovery update for the Old Farm and River Forest neighborhoods following Tropical Storm Chantal, reviewing flood impacts, door-to-door outreach, financial and process barriers, and resilience planning.

agenda_items.title: Council Announcements, Meeting Schedule Review & Agenda Settlement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council discussed scheduling conflicts for the September 21 meeting overlapping with Yom Kippur, reviewed administrative details, settled the evening's agenda, and adjourned the work session.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed via voice vote (unanimous motion to settle agenda)

votes.item_title: Comprehensive Plan Amendment A25002 Policy Changes
votes.discussion_detail: During the Durham City Council work session, the council considered procedural and agenda settlement items, including Comprehensive Plan Amendment A25002 policy changes and agenda adjustments for upcoming sessions. Council discussion preceding the vote touched on departmental efficiencies, neighborhood outreach programs, and scheduling adjustments for holidays such as Yom Kippur. The motion to approve and settle the agenda ultimately passed with a 4-3 vote. Nays were recorded by Nate Baker, Burrus, and Cook, reflecting contested viewpoints on specific administrative or procedural matters during the session.

meetings.title: Proposed Budget for Fiscal Year 2026-27 presented on May 18, 2026
meetings.executive_summary: Opening the May 18, 2026 special City Council meeting, Mayor Leonardo Williams emphasized that Council would strictly receive the manager's budget presentation with no votes or debate until upcoming work sessions and the June 1 public hearing. City Manager Bo Ferguson presented an unprecedented $766.1 million FY 2026-27 proposed budget featuring a $326.0 million General Fund—a $489,000 year-over-year decrease driven by over 10,000 countywide revaluation appeals reducing the tax base by ~$2.6 billion and requiring ~$5 million in General Fund ($9 million all-funds) refunds. Despite constrained revenues, the proposal holds the property tax rate flat at 43.71 cents per $100, raises water/sewer rates 12%, funds 2% pay-scale raises and a $25.09/hour livable wage (while omitting merit/step increases), commits $4.55 million toward a $13 million homelessness response, continues fare-free GoDurham via an $8.2 million County Transit transfer, closes Forest Hills Pool early, pauses standalone speed humps, cuts $927,000 in outside agency funding, and lays out a $798.4 million 10-year CIP.

agenda_items.title: Opening Remarks and Procedural Scope
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Leonardo Williams opened the session by clarifying that Council would take no votes or policy action on May 18 and would reserve formal comments and deliberation for budget work sessions and the June 1 public hearing.

agenda_items.title: FY 2026-27 Proposed Budget Presentation: Revenue Reset, Taxes, and Workforce Compensation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Bo Ferguson detailed how over 10,000 commercial and residential property tax appeals shrunk Durham's assessed base by ~$2.6 billion, producing Durham's first General Fund revenue contraction in recent memory ($326.0M vs $766.1M total budget) while still preserving AAA bond ratings via $2.2M fund balance usage and holding the tax rate flat at 43.71 cents ($1,853 median home tax bill). Water/sewer rates rise 12%, while employees receive 2% structural pay-scale raises, a 14% jump in the livable wage to $25.09/hour, absorbed health/dental increases, and a compensation study—balanced by suspending merit/step increases and eliminating 9 positions (4 vacant, 5 transitions) alongside 59 added or repurposed roles.

agenda_items.title: Public Safety, Reimagined Homelessness Strategy, and Fare-Free Transit Investments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Ferguson highlighted funding for 16 firefighter positions for delayed Ladder Company 8 activation, firefighter cancer screenings, and overtime, alongside a $4.55M City commitment in federal/ARPA interest funds toward a $13M Year-1 community homelessness plan ($9M rental assistance) targeting 30% unsheltered and 50% youth homelessness reductions plus $725K eviction diversion and $100K emergency home repairs. GoDurham fare-free service continues for one year through an $8.2M one-time Durham County Transit Plan contribution.

agenda_items.title: Service Reductions, $798.4M Capital Improvement Program (CIP), and Adoption Calendar
agenda_items.discussion_summary: To balance constrained operating revenues, the proposal closes Forest Hills Pool permanently before summer 2026, limits new speed humps to street resurfacing projects, and reduces or eliminates $927,000 in outside partner agency funding while maintaining a $798.4M 10-year CIP prioritizing Connect Durham paving/sidewalks, Jordan Lake Water Treatment Facility, PFAS upgrades, an Emergency Operations Center, and a Southeast Durham fire station. Mayor Williams closed by calling the budget 'an impossible deck of cards' ahead of May 27-28 work sessions and the June 1 public hearing.

meetings.title: Durham Joint City County Planning Committee (JCCPC) - May 6, 2026
meetings.executive_summary: At the May 6, 2026 JCCPC meeting chaired by Nate Baker, members excused the absences of County Commissioners Valentine and Burton, added an unscheduled UDO moratorium item proposed by Matt Kopac, and approved the April 1 minutes. EMS Chief Seth Kamansky and Planning staff revealed acute eastern-Durham EMS delays (14-18 minute response times on Cheek Road against a 9-minute target) and committed to adding EMS per-capita operational metrics into rezoning cover memos starting in August. After staff updates on the Braggtown/Oxford-Hamlin and Lakewood/West End/Lyon Park small area plans, sharp inter-jurisdictional conflict erupted over Item 7.5: County Commissioner Wendy Jacobs and County Attorney Curtis Massey protested the surprise UDO Section 3.19.6 moratorium repeal bypassing RTP stakeholders and Planning Commission review, while Mayor Pro Tem Javiera Caballero refused a slow three-month subcommittee and forced an expedited joint working group ahead of the June 15 Council and June 22 BOCC votes.

agenda_items.title: Roll Call, Excused Absences, Agenda Addition (Item 7.5), and Approval of April 1 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Nate Baker convened the meeting, where the committee unanimously excused absences for County Commissioners Stephen Valentine and Wendy Burton (note Vice Chair Mike Lee and Javiera Caballero joined later in the session) and unanimously approved the April 1, 2026 minutes. At Matt Kopac's request, the committee added Item 7.5 on amending UDO Section 3.19.6.C moratorium duration limits following Item 7.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Excused absences and April 1 minutes approved unanimously (voice votes)

agenda_items.title: Inclusion of EMS into Fiscal Impact Analysis (FIA)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Aaron Cain and EMS Chief Seth Kamansky presented emergency medical capacity constraints, reporting 14-18 minute EMS response times in east Durham (Cheek Rd) versus a 9-minute critical benchmark, a maximum fleet of 19 ambulances versus 41 fire apparatus, and 32-36 month waitlists for $500,000 ambulances. Planning staff committed to including EMS operational per-capita impact figures directly in rezoning staff-report cover memos starting in August rather than burying them inside the BMS spreadsheet.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Informational / Direction to integrate EMS impact into Aug staff memos

agenda_items.title: Braggtown Region and Oxford-Hamlin Small Area Plan Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Kayla Seibel and Scott Whiteman updated JCCPC on boundary sub-areas and two TOAs (Oxford Commons and Super Compare Foods) within the Braggtown small area plan. Matt Kopac highlighted absentee out-of-state landlord disrepair along State Street, Javiera Caballero emphasized preserving the Latino commercial corridor, and members discussed well/septic challenges near municipal limits and legal limits on downzoning.

agenda_items.title: Lakewood, West End, and Lyon Park Small Area Plan Pre-Draft Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Sarah Long briefed the committee on pre-draft engagement for the Lakewood, West End, and Lyon Park Small Area Plan, covering the Shops at Lakewood parcels (Brody Co. and Scrap Exchange), the pre-regulatory landfill beneath Lyon Park, and anti-displacement partnerships with DCLT and Al Futuro.

agenda_items.title: Data Center Moratorium UDO Section 3.19.6 Text Amendment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Matt Kopac and Nate Baker introduced revising UDO Section 3.19.6 to allow extending Durham's 60-day data center moratorium before its July 3 expiration, while Planning Director Sara Young recommended repealing Section 3.19.6.B onward entirely. County Commissioner Wendy Jacobs and County Attorney Curtis Massey criticized the last-minute addition lacking RTP/Treyburn and economic-development input and removing Planning Commission moratorium review; Mayor Pro Tem Caballero rejected a multi-month subcommittee, resulting in an immediate joint staff-elected working group ahead of June 9 PC, June 15 Council, and June 22 BOCC hearings.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Informational / Rapid joint City-County working group formed

agenda_items.title: FY26 Work Program Community Planning Projects
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff briefly confirmed no status changes to the FY26 Community Planning work program beyond the small area plan updates already presented before Chair Baker adjourned the meeting at 12:37 p.m.

votes.item_title: Excuse Absences for County Commissioners Stephen Valentine and Wendy Burton
votes.notes: Joint City-County Planning Committee procedural voice vote (transcript notes 'Commissioner Valentine and Burton', with Valentine attending a funeral); seconded 'in principle' and passed unanimously prior to arrivals of Javiera Caballero and Vice Chair Mike Lee.
votes.discussion_detail: At the start of the May 6, 2026 JCCPC meeting, Chair Nate Baker informed the committee of excused absence requests from County Commissioner Stephen Valentine (attending a funeral) and Commissioner Burton. Present members offered no objections, with one member noting a 'second in principle' to move the request forward. Before Mayor Pro Tem Javiera Caballero and Vice Chair Mike Lee arrived later in the session, present committee members—including Baker, Matt Kopac, and county/planning colleagues—approved the excused absences unanimously by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Approval of April 1, 2026 JCCPC Minutes
votes.notes: Joint City-County Planning Committee procedural voice vote; passed unanimously following agenda adjustment adding Item 7.5.
votes.discussion_detail: Immediately after adding Matt Kopac's Item 7.5 regarding UDO Section 3.19.6 moratorium limits to the agenda, Chair Nate Baker called for action on the minutes of the April 1, 2026 JCCPC meeting. Committee members had no edits or objections to the draft record. Following a motion and second, the minutes passed unanimously on an 'Aye' voice vote.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham Joint City County Planning Committee (JCCPC) - May 6, 2026
disagreements.issue: Process, Stakeholder Outreach, and Scope of UDO Section 3.19.6 Moratorium Text Amendment (Item 7.5)
disagreements.summary: City and County leaders clashed over Matt Kopac's surprise addition of a data-center moratorium UDO amendment and Planning staff's proposal to repeal all local caps and Planning Commission hearing rules in Section 3.19.6.B onward.
disagreements.side_a_position: Act decisively before the July 3 data center moratorium expires to prevent the 60-day pause from lapsing without permanent rules in place.
side_a_arguments: Matt Kopac and Nate Baker added Item 7.5 to ensure Council had legal authority to extend the data center moratorium past initial/12-month limits.

Javiera Caballero flatly refused to join a slow three-month subcommittee, insisting City Council had to act by June 15 ahead of the July 3 moratorium expiration and demanding that both attorneys and managers align in a single rapid meeting.
disagreements.side_b_position: Object to blindsiding County officials and RTP/Treyburn economic stakeholders and question eliminating Planning Commission review for all future moratoria.
side_b_arguments: County Commissioner Wendy Jacobs and County Attorney Curtis Massey protested the unvetted last-minute item introduced without consulting economic development directors, RTP, or County leadership.

County officials noted staff's draft went far beyond data centers by stripping Planning Commission public hearings and local duration caps across every future moratorium, and pressed for the City's draft language to be shared immediately.
disagreements.resolution: Staff proceeded with a staff-initiated repeal of Section 3.19.6.B onward (for June 9 PC, June 15 City Council, June 22 BOCC) while convening a single expedited joint working meeting with attorneys, planners, economic development directors, Jacobs, Nida Allam, and City representatives.
