meetings.title: Durham City Council May 4, 2026
meetings.presiding_chair: Leonardo Caballero (Mayor Pro Tem) / Leonardo Williams (Mayor)
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council held its regular meeting on May 4, 2026, issuing multiple ceremonial proclamations (Drinking Water Week, Taiwanese American Heritage Week, International Firefighters Day, and National Bike Month) and approving consent agenda items. The council adopted a 60-day temporary moratorium on data centers and cryptocurrency mining operations, approved economic development incentive agreements for AMAC Properties ($150,000) and CocoFro LLC ($115,000) along legacy commercial corridors, approved a consolidated annexation on South Miami Boulevard, and approved the consolidated annexation and rezoning (PDR 5.006) for the Enclave at Little Creek development with 20% affordable housing in a 4-2 split vote.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Proclamations and Council Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tem Caballero called the meeting to order, followed by a moment of silent meditation and the Pledge of Allegiance. Council received ceremonial proclamations for Drinking Water Week, Taiwanese American Heritage Week, International Firefighters Day, and National Bike Month, along with council member announcements and staff priority items.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The council reviewed and approved the consent agenda, which included performance audits, opioid settlement spending, HVAC upgrades, annual reports for Keep Durham Beautiful and Go Durham, budget amendments, and utility/infrastructure contracts.

agenda_items.title: Resolution to Set Public Hearing for Data Center Moratorium
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council took up a supplemental resolution to set a public hearing for a temporary moratorium on development approvals for data centers and cryptocurrency mining operations in the City of Durham.

agenda_items.title: Children's Wealth Building and Endangered Species Day Resolutions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public comment and ceremonial resolutions regarding Children's Wealth Building (savings accounts) and Endangered Species Day.

agenda_items.title: Temporary Moratorium on Data Centers and Crypto Mining
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Extensive public hearing and deliberation on imposing a temporary 60-day moratorium on development approvals for data centers and crypto mining operations. Numerous residents and advocates spoke on environmental, water, and energy grid impacts.

agenda_items.title: Economic Development Agreement - AMAC Properties, Inc.
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presentation and public hearing on an economic development incentive agreement with AMAC Properties, Inc. for the renovation of Marzella's Professional Complex at 2919 Fayetteville Street ($150,000 city funding).

agenda_items.title: Economic Development Agreement - CocoFro LLC
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presentation and public hearing on an economic development incentive agreement with CocoFro LLC for a freeze-dried ice cream production facility and tasting room at 1004 Morning Glory Avenue ($115,000 city funding).

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation - 1418 South Miami Boulevard
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public hearing on the consolidated voluntary annexation, utility extension agreement, and zoning consistency for two parcels totaling 3.44 acres at 1404 and 1418 South Miami Boulevard.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation & Rezoning - Enclave at Little Creek
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Major public hearing and contentious debate on the consolidated voluntary annexation, utility extension agreement, and rezoning (PDR 5.006 and RS-20) for 47.85 acres at 5524 and 5515 George King Road (Enclave at Little Creek) to allow up to 230 residential units with 20% affordable housing.

agenda_items.title: Revision to 2026 City Council Meeting Schedule
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Review and approval of supplemental agenda item to revise the 2026 City Council meeting schedule, rescheduling the May 7th work session to May 18th, 2026.

votes.item_title: Resolution to Set Public Hearing for Data Center Moratorium (Item 28)
votes.notes: Sets public hearing for temporary moratorium on data centers and crypto mining.
votes.discussion_detail: The council considered a resolution and associated procedural items to set a public hearing regarding a data center moratorium and related annexation and rezoning petitions. Discussions touched upon public hearing procedures, speaking time limits, and presentation materials from legal representatives such as Nil Ghosh regarding site constraints, natural heritage designations, and utility lift station infrastructure costs. Council members engaged in procedural management of public comments and meeting timelines. The motion was moved by Council Member Baker and seconded by Council Member Kopac, passing unanimously.

votes.item_title: Temporary Moratorium on Data Centers and Crypto Mining (Item 4)
votes.notes: Establishes 60-day moratorium pursuant to NCGS 160D-107.
votes.discussion_detail: The council considered an ordinance to adopt a temporary 60-day moratorium on development approvals for data centers, cryptocurrency mining operations, and associated processing facilities within the City of Durham pursuant to NCGS 160D-107. Council members discussed the lack of federal or state guidance and noted potential adverse impacts such as loud humming machinery near residential homes, low job creation, and poor land use compared to supporting local small businesses. Mayor Pro Tem Caballero and Mayor Williams highlighted regional organizing efforts and broader state-level legislative concerns regarding county water and grid usage. Following discussion, Council Member Rist moved and Council Member Burris seconded the motion to adopt the ordinance. The motion passed unanimously with no dissenting votes recorded.

votes.item_title: Economic Development Agreement - AMAC Properties, Inc. (Item 20)
votes.notes: Neighborhood revitalization grant for 2919 Fayetteville Street renovation.
votes.discussion_detail: The council evaluated an economic development agreement authorizing the city manager to execute a contract with AMAC Properties, Inc. in an amount not to exceed $150,000 for building renovations at 2919 Fayetteville Street. Speakers and council members emphasized supporting legacy businesses and small business ecosystems along the Fayetteville Street corridor, noting the property's five-decade history and its role as a microeconomic business hub and incubator. Council members Rist, Kopac, and Mayor Williams expressed support for neighborhood revitalization and local investment that avoids displacement. The motion was moved by Mayor Williams, seconded by Council Member Burris, and passed unanimously.

votes.item_title: Consolidated Annexation - 1418 South Miami Boulevard (Item 25)
votes.notes: Voluntary annexation of 3.44 acres with direct translational zoning.
votes.discussion_detail: The council considered a consolidated annexation and utility extension request for 1418 South Miami Boulevard, involving property annexation, zoning amendments from county to city jurisdiction for commercial general residential suburban-20 Falls/Jordan Watershed Overlay District B, and adoption of a consistency statement pursuant to NCGS 160D-605. Representatives for the property owner explained that the parcels are on the market and that neighborhood meetings had been held. Council members and staff reviewed satellite annexation policies, utility connections, and unified development ordinance standards. The motions were moved by Mayor Williams and Rist, seconded by Rist and Kopac, and passed unanimously across all votes.

votes.item_title: Consolidated Annexation & UEA - Enclave at Little Creek (Item 23) - Annexation & UEA
votes.notes: Annexation of 47.85 acres at 5524 and 5515 George King Road.
votes.discussion_detail: This motion proposed adopting an ordinance annexing the Enclave at Little Creek into the city of Durham and authorizing the city manager to enter into a utility extension agreement with Adobe Communities Acquisitions LLC. Council members debated the trade-offs of large-scale development, affordability components, and environmental conservation, referencing prior votes on Vision Zero, the comprehensive plan, and transportation planning. Council Member Caballero supported the case largely due to its high affordability component and lack of city subsidy. Conversely, dissenting members Nate Baker and Carl R. Burris opposed the motion, reflecting ongoing concerns regarding walkability standards, urban form, and the departure from desired growth patterns prior to the formal adoption of the LDC. The motion ultimately passed with a 4-2 vote, with Council Members Baker and Burris voting no.

votes.item_title: Consolidated Annexation - Enclave at Little Creek (Item 23) - UDO PDR 5.006 Amendment
votes.notes: Rezoning to PDR 5.006 for up to 230 residential units with 20% affordable housing.
votes.discussion_detail: This motion proposed amending the unified development ordinance to take property out of the residential suburban-20 Falls/Jordan Watershed Overlay B county jurisdiction and establish it as planned development residential 5.006 Falls/Jordan Watershed Overlay B city jurisdiction for the Enclave at Little Creek project. The discussion preceding the vote touched on balancing density, walkability, affordability, and environmental protections. Supporters emphasized the lack of city subsidies and the inclusion of strong affordability elements, while opponents maintained consistency with their positions on managing forested and large-scale properties. The motion passed 4-2, with Nate Baker and Carl R. Burris voting in the negative.

votes.item_title: Consolidated Annexation - Enclave at Little Creek (Item 23) - UDO RS-20 Amendment
votes.notes: Translational zoning for the second parcel to city RS-20.
votes.discussion_detail: This motion proposed amending the unified development ordinance to take property out of the residential suburban-20 Falls/Jordan Watershed Overlay B county jurisdiction and establish it as residential suburban-20 Falls/Jordan Watershed Overlay B city jurisdiction as part of the Enclave at Little Creek consolidated annexation and UDO changes. The item followed earlier debate regarding community concerns, public goods, and the appropriate regulatory standards for urban expansion in Durham. Council Members Nate Baker and Carl R. Burris voted against the zoning designation change, while the majority approved the motion 4-2.

votes.item_title: Consolidated Annexation - Enclave at Little Creek (Item 23) - Consistency Statement
votes.notes: Required consistency statement under NCGS 160D-605.
votes.discussion_detail: This motion proposed adopting a consistency statement as required by North Carolina General Statutes Section 160D-605 in connection with the Enclave at Little Creek annexation and UDO amendments. Following the roll-call votes on the preceding annexation and zoning ordinance motions, the council voted unanimously to adopt the statutory consistency statement.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham City Council May 4, 2026
disagreements.issue: Enclave at Little Creek Annexation and Rezoning (Item 23)
disagreements.summary: Debate over the 47.85-acre Enclave at Little Creek annexation and rezoning (PDR 5.006) for up to 230 residential units with 20% affordable housing versus environmental and infrastructure concerns in the Jordan Lake watershed.
disagreements.side_a_position: Support annexation and rezoning for the Enclave at Little Creek development.
side_a_arguments: Durham has an acute housing shortage and rising home prices, requiring increased housing density.
The project includes 20% income-restricted affordable housing, exceeding standard city goals.
The proposal aligns with the comprehensive plan's designation for mixed residential development near transit opportunity areas.
If denied, the property could be developed as low-density single-family estates on well and septic without any affordable housing commitments.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose annexation and rezoning due to environmental impact, infrastructure strain, and stormwater risks.
side_b_arguments: Significant environmental and ecological concerns regarding impacts on the natural heritage area and Jordan Lake watershed headwaters.
Stormwater runoff and drainage issues affecting downstream neighborhoods during drought and heavy rain events.
Inadequate walkability, lack of sidewalks, and distance from public transit and amenities.
Concerns that the 20% affordable housing is structured as a separate standalone component rather than fully integrated inclusionary housing.
disagreements.resolution: Passed (4-2)

meetings.title: Durham City Council Work Session April 23, 2026
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council held its Work Session on April 23, 2026, presided over by Mayor Williams. The meeting included tributes to retiring Police Chief Patrice Andrews, an update on the regional drought conditions by Water Management Director Don Greeley, public comments regarding local development and sediment controls, and the suspension of rules to vote on vehicle purchases. The council also discussed and settled upcoming agenda items, moving several resolutions to the General Business Agenda (GBA).

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call & Council Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Durham City Council Work Session was called to order at 1:00 PM by Mayor Williams. Roll call established the presence of Mayor Williams, Mayor Pro Tem Caballero, and Council Members Baker, Burris, Cook, and Kopack, with Council Member Rist excused. Council members shared brief opening announcements and approved excused absences for upcoming meetings.
agenda_items.vote_summary: No formal vote (routine absence votes passed by voice vote)

agenda_items.title: Recognition of Retiring Police Chief Patrice Andrews
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Ryan Smith, Mayor Williams, and council members offered heartfelt tributes honoring retiring Police Chief Patrice Andrews for her 25 years of service in Durham and 30 years in law enforcement. Chief Andrews delivered emotional remarks reflecting on her career, community trust-building, and the evolution of policing in Durham. Incoming interim chief Walter Tate was also briefly introduced.

agenda_items.title: Manager's Priority Items: Drought Status & Technology Leadership
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Ryan Smith introduced Richard Barbee as the new Director of Technology Solutions and commended interim director Marcia Richardson. Water Management Director Don Greeley provided a status update on the ongoing drought, noting that Durham County entered extreme drought conditions while lake levels are at 84%, and discussed regional utility coordination.

agenda_items.title: Public Comments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Members of the public, including Trina Hymes representing Grove Park Homeowners Association, addressed the council regarding stormwater runoff and topographical ridge protection concerning development sites near Little Lick Creek. Other scheduled speakers deferred their comments to upcoming public hearings.

agenda_items.title: Purchase of Tandem Axle Dump Trucks (Transource Inc.)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City council considered and approved a motion to suspend the rules to immediately vote on two equipment purchase items due to pending price increases. Council authorized contracts with Transource Inc. of Kernersville, NC, for purchasing tandem axle dump trucks for the fleet.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed, 6-0 (Motion to suspend rules passed; Item 6 passed 6-0; Item 7 passed 6-0)

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Review: Resolutions & Policy Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council reviewed pulled consent agenda items, discussing the Children's Wealth Building Resolution (Item 2), Endangered Species Day Resolution (Item 3), and proposed temporary development moratorium on data centers and cryptocurrency mining facilities (Item 4). Council members debated details and agreed to move several policy resolutions to the General Business Agenda (GBA).
agenda_items.vote_summary: No formal vote (items moved to General Business Agenda for later consideration)

agenda_items.title: Accessible Pedestrian Signals & Work Zone Safety Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Transportation Director Sean Egan presented construction contracts and updates regarding signalized pedestrian upgrades across 13 locations, incorporating accessible pedestrian signals (APS) and leading pedestrian intervals. Staff also highlighted roadway work zone safety awareness week, urging drivers to exercise caution and slow down in work zones.

agenda_items.title: GoDurham Fiscal Year Annual Report & Transit Operations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council reviewed the GoDurham annual report, praising system performance metrics compared to peer cities while discussing fleet age, preventative maintenance contractor performance issues, and regional transit funding shortfalls discussed at joint city-county meetings.

agenda_items.title: Water & Sewer Fund Budget Ordinance Amendment & Agenda Settlement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Don Greeley and budget staff presented a budget ordinance amendment for water and sewer funds, explaining fund balance transfers required due to reduced vacancy savings as positions were successfully filled. Council subsequently settled the final meeting agenda and adjourned the work session at 2:48 PM.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed, 6-0 (Motion to settle agenda passed; meeting adjourned)

votes.item_title: Purchase of five tandem axle dump trucks (Transource Inc.) - Item 6
votes.discussion_detail: Following a motion to suspend the rules, the City Council voted to authorize a contract with Transource Incorporated of Kernersville, North Carolina, for the purchase of five tandem axle dump trucks in the total amount of $1,467,751.75. The motion was moved by Mayor Williams, seconded by Council Member Baker, and passed unanimously (6-0).

votes.item_title: Purchase of five tandem axle dump trucks (Transource Inc.) - Item 7
votes.discussion_detail: Immediately following the previous item, the council considered and approved a second contract with Transource Incorporated of Kernersville, North Carolina, for the purchase of an additional five tandem axle dump trucks totaling $1,270,368,000. The motion was moved by Mayor Williams, seconded by Council Member Baker, and passed unanimously (6-0) following the suspension of the rules.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham City Council April 20, 2026
disagreements.issue: Morgan Farm Annexation and Residential Development Proposal (MI Homes)
disagreements.summary: Debate over whether to approve the annexation and utility extension for a 300+ unit residential development (Morgan Farm) on a sensitive forested site within the Jordan/Falls Lake watershed.
disagreements.side_a_position: Support annexation and development
side_a_arguments: The developer made unprecedented commitments including 50% open space conservation, 8% affordable housing at 80% AMI, and $2 million in transportation and intersection improvements.
Denying annexation leaves landowners with little choice but to timber/log the property or develop with wells and septic without city oversight or conservation benefits.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose annexation and development
side_b_arguments: The site has high environmental sensitivity (Triassic Basin soils, steep slopes, proximity to Panther/Little Creek, Falls/Jordan Lake protected watershed).
Translational zoning lacks enforceable protections and stormwater commitments at the rezoning stage, and the Planning Commission voted 9-0 against it.
Inadequate local infrastructure including fire/EMS response times, sewer capacity, and severe traffic congestion on local roads.
disagreements.resolution: The motion to approve annexation and utility extension failed 5-2.

agenda_items.title: Evaluation and Assessment Report (EAR) Phase 1: Place-Type Map and Policy Edits

After Planning Commission Chair Chagaris noted a tense 7-4 PC vote and members discovered the PDF stripped Word track-changes, Jacobs, Valentine, Burris, and Kopac secured a hold on the policy edits for a four-member subcommittee while advancing the map updates.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Direction to advance place-type map changes; policy edits held for 4-member subcommittee (Jacobs, Valentine, Burris, Kopac)

agenda_items.title: EAR Phase 2 Technical Data Preview (Rezonings, Policy Compliance & Affordable Proffers)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Principal Planner Andy Lester demonstrated an internal database tracking every rezoning since 2020, 30+ policy compliance scores since 2023, and affordable housing proffers (most commonly 5%, 8%, and seven 100%-affordable cases), now shared with Neighborhood Improvement Services (NIS) to track covenant recordation, building permits, and COs. Javiera Caballero and Wendy Jacobs urged tracking 30-year covenant expiration dates and pursuing City/County right-of-first-refusal clauses to preserve affordability long-term.

agenda_items.title: FY 2027 Planning Work Program Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning Director Sara Young presented the final draft FY27 Work Program retaining the LDC rewrite and adding six items: Walltown small area plan paper-street closings (pending surveyor funding), natural resource protection overlays research, tree canopy assessment recommendations, Biophilic Cities metrics, Urban Design Studios revival, and Clarity permitting software replacing the 2007 LDO platform. Following a question on Walltown survey funding, the committee voted unanimously to recommend the work program to both governing bodies.

agenda_items.title: FY26 Work Program Community Planning Projects
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Bo Dobrzenski briefly reviewed the Gantt chart tracker for ongoing FY26 Community Planning work, noting Lakewood engagement events (April 16 and May 7 on Shops at Lakewood), Greater Braggtown outreach, the Open Space Plan, Orange Factory Heritage Community story map, and the 10-year Historic Properties inventory update before adjournment at 10:57 a.m.

votes.item_title: Approval of April 1, 2026 JCCPC Agenda as Presented
votes.notes: Joint City-County Planning Committee voice vote; JCCPC Vice Chair Mike Lee presided (Chair Nate Baker excused) alongside Planning Commission Chair Chagaris and County Commissioner Stephen Valentine. Javiera Caballero arrived immediately after this vote at 00:03:57.
votes.discussion_detail: Opening the April 1, 2026 JCCPC session in the excused absence of Chair Nate Baker, Vice Chair Mike Lee called roll and confirmed a quorum with City Council members Matt Kopac and Shanetta Burris alongside Planning Commission Chair Chagaris and County Commissioner Stephen Valentine. Lee asked if any member wished to adjust the agenda as circulated. Hearing no requested modifications, a motion and second were made to adopt the agenda as presented, which passed unanimously via voice vote just moments before Mayor Pro Tem Javiera Caballero took her seat.

votes.item_title: Approval of March 4, 2026 JCCPC Minutes
votes.notes: Joint City-County Planning Committee voice vote; Vice Chair Mike Lee, Planning Commission Chair Chagaris, and County Commissioner Stephen Valentine also present and voting Aye.
votes.discussion_detail: After noting Mayor Pro Tem Javiera Caballero's arrival and confirming no announcements were needed, Vice Chair Mike Lee placed the March 4, 2026 JCCPC minutes before the committee for formal approval. No committee member offered corrections or requested edits to the draft minutes. A motion and second were offered without discussion, and all present members—including City Council members Caballero, Matt Kopac, and Shanetta Burris—approved the minutes unanimously on a voice vote.

votes.item_title: Recommend Approval of FY 2027 Planning Department Work Program to Governing Bodies
votes.notes: Joint City-County Planning Committee vote recommending the FY27 Work Program to Durham City Council and the Durham County Board of Commissioners per the Interlocal Agreement; County Commissioners Lee, Jacobs, and Valentine and PC Chair Chagaris also present.
votes.discussion_detail: Planning Director Sara Young walked JCCPC through the final draft FY 2027 Planning Work Program, which retains the Land Development Code (LDC) rewrite and adds six new items: Walltown small area plan paper-street closings, natural resource protection overlays research, tree canopy assessment recommendations, Biophilic Cities metrics tracking, revival of Urban Design Studios charettes, and implementation of the Clarity cloud permitting portal to replace the 2007 LDO system. A committee member asked why the Walltown paper-street item carried a pending-funding caveat, and Young explained that hiring outside surveyors could face tight budget constraints unless funds are identified elsewhere. With no further objections or amendments, a motion and second were made to recommend the drafted FY27 Work Program to the City Council and County Commission, passing unanimously on an 'Aye' voice vote.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham Joint City County Planning Committee (JCCPC) - April 1, 2026
disagreements.issue: EAR Comprehensive Plan Policy Deletions/Edits: Scope of 'Technical' Changes and Review Pace
disagreements.summary: Committee members pushed back strongly against advancing staff's proposed Phase 1 Evaluation and Assessment Report (EAR) policy edits to the governing bodies within two weeks, arguing the changes were substantive rather than technical and lacked visible redlines.
disagreements.side_a_position: Slow down the EAR policy package, restore full Word track-changes and public/advisory board comments, and examine substantive gaps in rural, farmland, EMS, and DPS evaluations.
side_a_arguments: County Commissioner Wendy Jacobs rejected characterizing 21 deleted policies and 28 edited policies as mere 'technical changes,' noting residents spent years crafting the 2023 Comprehensive Plan and deserve full written comments and a dedicated committee review.
Jacobs also urged using the EAR to strengthen policies on out-of-UGB annexations, farmland loss, county EMS costs, and Durham Public Schools operational funding.

Matt Kopac flagged that the packet PDF stripped out most redline track-changes, preventing due diligence, while Shanetta Burris and County Commissioner Stephen Valentine backed slowing the process and auditing rural/agricultural map impacts.
disagreements.side_b_position: Clarify that removed policies merely eliminate automatic 'free checks' for mandatory UDO/ADA standards while allowing an optional two-week turnaround if ready.
side_b_arguments: Planning staff (Aaron Cain and Payton Burgess) explained that removing policies already codified in the UDO (such as mass grading or ADA compliance) was meant to prevent staff reports from inflating developer consistency scores rather than relaxing rules, and invited JCCPC feedback within two weeks for next month's agenda if feasible.
disagreements.resolution: Staff agreed to advance only the six place-type map updates immediately while pausing all EAR policy edits for an ad hoc subcommittee of Wendy Jacobs, Stephen Valentine, Shanetta Burris, and Matt Kopac with full track-change Word files and written board feedback.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council members shared opening announcements, including Councilmember Copek mentioning the Environmental Affairs Board letter on Duke Energy's carbon plan, Councilmember Wrist highlighting March Madness and upcoming parks bond public meetings, and the Mayor Pro Tem discussing the reporting on Cesar Chavez and community survivors.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation for Cleaning Week (General Services Custodial Team)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Leonardo Williams and the city council recognized the General Services Department custodial team and celebrated upcoming International Cleaning Week (cleaning week in Durham), highlighting the city's commitment to in-house cleaning staff with competitive wages and benefits rather than third-party outsourcing.

agenda_items.title: Priority Items, City Attorney Introduction, and Board & Committee Reports
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager reported no priority items for the City Manager's Office. Cole, Lena G. Tonkan, Nicholas Monton, Priesty Willis) and noted lack of consensus for the Human Relations Commission appointment.

meetings.title: Durham City Council March 16, 2026 (Full Audio)
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council held its regular meeting on March 16, 2026, featuring several proclamations, public hearings on the upcoming FY 2027 budget and CIP, and votes on capital financing and zoning changes. The council debated and approved amendments to the Fayetteville Street Corridor Neighborhood Stabilization Partnership and grant agreement with Hataway Promise Community Development Corporation (removing St. Joseph's Historic Foundation as fiscal agent) in a 5-2 split vote. Additionally, the council unanimously approved a $136 million limited obligation bond resolution for capital projects, solid waste, and DPAC HVAC reimbursements, as well as a zoning map change for 1612 and 1562 Carpenter Fletcher Road.

agenda_items.title: Opening, Pledge of Allegiance & Roll Call
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor pro tem opened the meeting, followed by a moment of silent meditation, the Pledge of Allegiance, and roll call confirming council members present.

agenda_items.title: Proclamations & Special Presentations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council members read and presented proclamations for Bleeding Disorders Awareness Month, Durham Crop Hunger Walk, and International Women's History Month.

agenda_items.title: Council Member Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council members shared community updates, recognized local sports achievements (Southern High School 7A state championship), and highlighted upcoming events and creek cleanups.

agenda_items.title: Fayetteville Street Corridor Stabilization & Hataway Promise CDC Grant Agreement Amendments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Extensive public comments and council debate regarding the first amendment to the ARPA/Revenue Recovery Subrecipient Grant Agreement and Fayetteville Street Corridor Neighborhood Stabilization Partnership with Hataway Promise CDC and St. Joseph's Historic Foundation. Discussion focused on fiscal oversight, transparency, community engagement, and progress tracking.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed (5-2 on Item 12.1; unanimous on subsequent modifications and partnership amendments).

agenda_items.discussion_summary: City debt administrator presented the proposed limited obligation bond series 2026AB (not to exceed $136 million) to fund general capital projects, solid waste, and DPAC HVAC project costs. Public hearing was held with no speakers signed up.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed unanimously (Unanimous vote on installment financing contract resolution and legal document execution).

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff and applicant presented a zoning map change request for 1612 and 1562 Carpenter Fletcher Road from Commercial General with textual development plan and office/institutional to Commercial General with textual development plan to expand permitted uses and commit to native landscaping species.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed unanimously (Unanimous vote on zoning map ordinance and consistency statement).

agenda_items.title: FY 2027 Budget & Capital Improvement Plan Public Hearing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Budget and Management Services director presented the public hearing to receive comments on the development of the FY 2027 budget and FY 2027-2032 Capital Improvement Plan (CIP).

votes.item_title: First Amendment to ARPA/Revenue Recovery Subrecipient Grant Agreement with Hataway Promise Community Development Corporation
votes.notes: Removes St. Joseph's Historic Foundation as fiscal agent and updates funding source up to $6,755,000.
votes.discussion_detail: This vote concerned the first amendment to the ARPA/Revenue Recovery Subrecipient Grant Agreement with Hataway Promise Community Development Corporation, involving a total amount not to exceed $6,755,000 to remove St. Joseph's Historic Foundation Inc. as fiscal agent and change the funding source. Council members debated major work products, reporting intervals, and community engagement, with Council Member Baker requesting reports at 6- to 12-month intervals until funds are fully expended. The motion passed 5-2, with Council Members Burrus and Cook voting in opposition.

votes.item_title: Subsequent Modifications Authorization for Hataway Promise CDC Grant Agreement
votes.notes: Authorizes city manager to negotiate and make subsequent modifications up to $6,755,000.
votes.discussion_detail: This routine motion authorized the city manager to negotiate and make subsequent modifications to the amended grant agreement with Hataway Promise Community Development Corporation, provided that total grant funds do not exceed $6,755,000. The motion passed unanimously without recorded debate or opposition.

votes.item_title: Fayetteville Street Corridor Neighborhood Stabilization Partnership Agreement Amendment
votes.notes: First amendment involving Hataway Promise CDC, City of Durham, and Preserving Home Inc. to remove St. Joseph Historic Foundation as fiscal agent.
votes.discussion_detail: This vote authorized the first amendment to the agreement between Hataway Promise Community Development Corporation, the City of Durham, and Preserving Home Inc. (formerly Rebuilding Together of the Triangle Inc.) for the Fayetteville Street corridor neighborhood stabilization partnership implementation. The amendment removed St. Joseph Historic Foundation Inc. as fiscal agent. The motion passed unanimously.

votes.item_title: Limited Obligation Bonds Series 2026AB Installment Financing Contract
votes.notes: Approving installment financing contract not to exceed $136 million for general capital, solid waste, and DPAC HVAC project costs.
votes.discussion_detail: This vote adopted a resolution approving an installment financing contract not to exceed $136 million along with an accompanying deed of trust, and provided for a public hearing concerning the contract to finance general capital, solid waste, and DPAC (Durham Arts) needs as presented by debt administrator John Reese. The motion passed unanimously.

votes.item_title: Execution of Legal Documents for 2026AB Limited Obligation Bonds
votes.notes: Authorizing city manager/designate to execute associated legal documents.
votes.discussion_detail: Following the adoption of the financing contract, this vote authorized the city manager or his designate to execute other associated legal documents and make pre-execution changes consistent with the intent of the agenda item memo and existing document versions. The motion passed unanimously.

votes.item_title: Zoning Map Change for 1612 and 1562 Carpenter Fletcher Road
votes.notes: Expanding permitted uses under Commercial General with textual development plan, including commitment to native species landscaping.
votes.discussion_detail: The council considered a zoning map change for 1612 and 1562 Carpenter Fletcher Road, amending the unified development ordinance to transition property out of commercial general with a textual development plan in office and institutional and establishing the same as commercial general with the textual development plan. Prior to the vote, discussion centered on landscaping commitments, with a council member asking for confirmation regarding the inclusion of native plant species. Staff confirmed they would work with the applicant the following day to secure official language committing to native species for future site landscaping changes and redevelopment. Following this clarification, the motion to adopt the ordinance was moved, seconded, and passed unanimously with zero nays.

votes.item_title: Consistency Statement for 1612 and 1562 Carpenter Fletcher Road Zoning Change
votes.notes: Statutory consistency statement under NCGS 160D-605.
votes.discussion_detail: Following the approval of the zoning map change for 1612 and 1562 Carpenter Fletcher Road, the council considered the mandatory consistency statement as required by North Carolina General Statute section 160D-605. The motion to adopt the consistency statement was duly moved and seconded. The clerk opened and closed the vote, and the motion passed unanimously with no opposition.

disagreements.issue: Fayetteville Street Corridor Stabilization Partnership & Hataway Promise CDC Grant Amendment
disagreements.summary: Debate over amending the Fayetteville Street corridor stabilization grant agreement to remove St. Joseph's Historic Foundation as fiscal agent and allocate funds up to $6,755,000 to Hataway Promise CDC.
disagreements.side_a_position: Support moving forward with the agreement and removing St. Joseph's Historic Foundation as fiscal agent.
side_a_arguments: Stated that Hataway Promise CDC has shown meaningful progress, that strict metrics and reporting intervals (six-month updates) are established, and that further delay would stall much-needed investment and restitution in a historically disinvested corridor.
disagreements.side_b_position: Voted against the agreement out of concern for financial oversight and accountability, while clarifying support for the corridor community.

disagreements.resolution: Passed 5-2, with Council Members Burrus and Cook voting against.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Work Session March 5, 2026
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council held its work session on March 5, 2026, discussing critical infrastructure and community development items, including a wastewater collection system capacity overview highlighting capacity constraints in the Goose Creek basin and upcoming infrastructure projects, as well as an implementation update on the Fayetteville Street Corridor Neighborhood Stabilization Partnership involving Hayti Promise CDC. The council also heard extensive public comments on unpaved streets, traffic fatalities, park encampments, and gun violence, settled the meeting agenda, and voted to enter a closed session for attorney-client consultation and property damage claims.

agenda_items.title: Roll Call, Announcements, and Opening Remarks
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Williams called the work session to order, followed by a roll call and brief council announcements, including updates on joint city-county planning, environmental boards, and birthday wishes for Councilmember Kopac. agenda_items.title: Manager and Attorney Priorities & Closed Session Motion

agenda_items.title: DPAC Oversight Committee Mayoral Appointment

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Reading and Item Pulls
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Mayor read the consent agenda items, and councilmembers discussed and pulled specific items for separate discussion and public comment (including items 10, 12, 13, and 14).

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Residents spoke during citizen matters on various topics, including unpaved street and water infrastructure needs on Ottmar Drive, traffic safety and district attorney accountability regarding hit-and-run fatalities, park encampments at Oakwood Park, and gun violence prevention.

agenda_items.title: Wastewater Collection System Capacity Overview Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City staff delivered a comprehensive presentation on wastewater collection system capacity, focusing on the unexpected 100% capacity finding in the Goose Creek basin, ongoing outfall improvement projects, hydraulic modeling, and the issuance of Letters to Industry (LTIs) restricting development. agenda_items.title: Fayetteville Street Corridor Project Implementation Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff and representatives presented an update on the Fayetteville Street Corridor Neighborhood Stabilization Partnership Implementation, detailing the deployment of ARPA funds, historic preservation partnerships (Preservation Durham, Preserving Home Inc.), youth workforce training, and governance structures of the Hayti Promise CDC. agenda_items.title: Settle Agenda for Forthcoming Meeting

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham City Council Work Session March 5, 2026
disagreements.issue: Communication and notification transparency regarding wastewater capacity Letters to Industry in the Goose Creek basin
disagreements.summary: Councilmembers debated whether issuing letters to industry restricting development due to sewer capacity constraints without direct mailings to affected property owners was sufficient.
disagreements.side_a_position: Standard administrative practice via industry associations is sufficient.
side_a_arguments: LTIs were distributed through standard channels like the Home Builders Association and voluntary sign-up lists, consistent with past practice.
disagreements.side_b_position: Direct mailings or expanded property records outreach should be used to notify affected property owners.
side_b_arguments: Property owners were caught by surprise with halted development rights without direct notice or due process.
disagreements.resolution: Staff agreed to evaluate expanding notification methods and budgetary impacts for property-specific letters to industry in the future.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham City Council Work Session March 5, 2026
disagreements.issue: Accountability, structure, and oversight of ARPA funding and community development for the Fayetteville Street Corridor (Hayti Promise CDC)
disagreements.summary: Councilmembers and community members debated the effectiveness, administrative hurdles, and oversight surrounding the Hayti Promise CDC and ARPA investments.
disagreements.side_a_position: Supportive of the bold ARPA investment and volunteer board efforts.

disagreements.side_b_position: Expressed caution and concern over administrative overhead, financial controls, and accountability.
side_b_arguments: High consultant expenditures, lack of established organizational capacity, and questions over financial transparency raised red flags.
disagreements.resolution: Discussion concluded with consensus on maintaining oversight, auditing future expenditures, and supporting ongoing corridor revitalization efforts while demanding accountability.

meetings.title: Durham Joint City County Planning Committee (JCCPC) - March 3, 2026
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Nate Baker convened the March 3, 2026 JCCPC meeting with Javiera Caballero excused, where members unanimously approved the February 4 minutes and received a brief update from Planning Director Sara Young confirming the new LDC/UDO remained paused with no new timeline. Staff previewed two major residential annexations inside the UGB—the 323.79-acre Laurel Creek project (up to 1,520 units plus commercial and a fire station site) and 35.52-acre Massey Chapel Assemblage (up to 470 units)—followed by Three Oaks Engineering's kickoff of the Multimodal TIA methodology and Durham Parks and Recreation's (DPR) overhaul of its Land Acquisition and Acceptance Policy integrating social/environmental equity scores. The meeting closed with sharp criticism from County Commissioner Wendy Jacobs over outside-UGB rezoning staff reports (specifically Cheek Road) ignoring farmland loss and EMS/fire response realities, winning broad agreement to overhaul large-case staff reports.

agenda_items.title: Roll Call, Approval of February 4 Minutes, and LDC/UDO Pause Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Nate Baker called roll with Vice Chair Mike Lee, Matt Kopac, Planning Commission Chair Chagaris, and Commissioner Stephen Valentine present (Javiera Caballero excused; Wendy Jacobs arrived at 00:08:06 and Shanetta Burris arrived shortly thereafter). The committee unanimously approved the February 4, 2026 minutes and heard Planning Director Sara Young confirm the LDC rewrite remained paused with no set schedule after converting the prior week's Planning Commission hearing into an informational session.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Case Preview (Laurel Creek & Massey Chapel Road Assemblage)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Javon Jones previewed two cases inside the UGB proposed for city annexation: Laurel Creek (323.79 acres off Copper Depot/Camp/Old Camp Roads, RR to PDR 4.402 for up to 1,520 units, 25,000 sq ft commercial, and a proffered fire station via satellite annexation) and Massey Chapel Road Assemblage (35.52 acres, RR to PDR 18.021 for up to 470 townhouse/apartment units via contiguous annexation). Commissioner Wendy Jacobs asked staff to ensure eastern Durham EMS impacts are analyzed on Laurel Creek.

agenda_items.title: Multimodal Traffic Impact Analysis (TIA) Project Introduction
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Lisa Miller and Three Oaks Engineering consultant Jennifer Baldwin introduced the six-month effort (targeting an August draft ordinance) to build a legally defensible multimodal TIA under North Carolina law, likely using a hybrid NCDOT/City model and point-based metric tied to the 2025 Vision Zero Action Plan and High Injury Network. Members urged aligning with Triangle West TPO's Destination 2055 MTP to measure moving people rather than cars (Jacobs), targeting 'urban triage' corridors (Baker), and testing past cases.

agenda_items.title: Durham Parks and Recreation (DPR) Land Acquisition and Acceptance Policy
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DPR Senior Planner Austin Bowman presented the updated Land Acquisition and Acceptance Policy replacing suitability-only screening with a two-tier evaluation (Community Need via an Investment Priority Indicator plus Strategic Value, followed by Suitability) and previewed a five-tier proactive Land Acquisition Strategy. Committee members broadly praised the shift and pressed staff on minimum pocket-park sizing (Burris), county park coordination and land banking (Jacobs), developer template proffers and park proximity (Kopac), urban plazas and outdated 2009/2013 park impact fees (Baker), and setting bold expectations for developers (Valentine).

agenda_items.title: FY26 Community Planning Work Program Tracker
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Scott Whiteman presented the monthly Community Planning project tracker, highlighting the newly launched Orange Factory Heritage Community designation in North Durham—Durham's second after Merrick-Moore—and clarifying fiscal-year quarter labels for the committee.

agenda_items.title: Out-of-UGB / Large Annexation Staff Reports, Farmland Impacts, and EMS Analysis
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Added at Commissioner Wendy Jacobs's request, JCCPC debated systemic flaws in planning staff reports for outside-UGB and large rural annexations—specifically the Cheek Road rezoning—citing missing farmland-protection weight, conflicts with the County's $450K Golden LEAF farm campus investment, omitted EMS metrics, and misleading fire proximity claims (13-minute city fire vs adjacent Redwood VFD mutual-aid limits). Baker, Valentine, and Kopac endorsed placing staff-report reform on a future JCCPC agenda before adjournment at 11:43 a.m.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Informational / Consensus to schedule staff-report reform on future agenda

votes.item_title: Approval of February 4, 2026 JCCPC Minutes
votes.notes: Joint City-County Planning Committee voice vote; Vice Chair Mike Lee, Planning Commission Chair Chagaris, and County Commissioner Stephen Valentine also voted Aye. Mayor Pro Tem Javiera Caballero was excused, and Wendy Jacobs and Shanetta Burris arrived shortly after the vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Chair Nate Baker convened the March 3, 2026 JCCPC meeting with Mayor Pro Tem Javiera Caballero excused and County Commissioners Wendy Jacobs and Council Member Shanetta Burris en route. Following roll call and a brief agenda adjustment scheduling a status update on the paused LDC/UDO under priority items, Baker called for approval of the February 4, 2026 minutes. No edits or objections were offered by the members present. A motion to approve and a second carried unanimously by voice vote among Baker, Matt Kopac, Vice Chair Mike Lee, Chair Chagaris, and Commissioner Stephen Valentine.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham Joint City County Planning Committee (JCCPC) - March 3, 2026
disagreements.issue: Staff Report Adequacy for Out-of-UGB Annexations, Rural Farmland Loss, and County EMS/Fire Response (Cheek Road)
disagreements.summary: County Commissioner Wendy Jacobs sharply criticized existing rezoning staff reports for failing to weigh annexation criteria, farmland preservation, and county emergency response impacts equally against generic checkboxes, highlighting the Cheek Road rezoning.
disagreements.side_a_position: Reform staff reports immediately to weight out-of-UGB annexation criteria, incorporate County Farmland/Open Space boards, reflect real EMS/mutual-aid fire realities, and oppose incompatible out-of-UGB rezonings like Cheek Road.
side_a_arguments: Jacobs argued all 30 Comp Plan policies are treated as equal checklists in staff reports, omitting policies protecting farmland even as Durham County invests $450,000 in Golden LEAF grants and a 100-acre farm campus.
Jacobs noted Cheek Road staff reports lacked EMS impact analysis and relied on a 13-minute city fire station response while ignoring mutual-aid limits with the adjacent Redwood Fire Department.
Nate Baker and Commissioner Stephen Valentine endorsed adding qualitative food/childcare-desert, farmland, and county-representation analyses to large-case staff reports.
disagreements.side_b_position: Acknowledge the value of improved staff-report usability and emergency data while recognizing city-county coordination limits and balancing staff workload.
side_b_arguments: Matt Kopac welcomed future staff-report improvements and noted staff reports need clear, digestible information for elected officials alongside existing planning frameworks.
disagreements.resolution: Chair Baker agreed to work with Planning Director Sara Young to place a comprehensive review of rezoning/annexation staff reports on an upcoming JCCPC agenda.

meetings.title: Durham City Council March 2, 2026

agenda_items.title: City Council Member Announcements & Regional Updates
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council members shared announcements regarding local business incubator openings, labor union events, community health fairs, condolences for fallen state trooper Steven Perry, concerns over ongoing conflicts in the Middle East, and upcoming budget retreat priorities and public hearings.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 1-11, 13-14)

agenda_items.title: City Manager's Budget Outlook and Opening Remarks
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Bo Ferguson delivered candid opening remarks expressing serious stress regarding the FY2026/2027 revenue and expenditure outlook, noting that revenue projections are underperforming while expenditure pressures are mounting. meetings.title: Durham City Council Budget Retreat: Day 2 - Friday, February 27, 2026 - Part 3
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council held Day 2 of their 2026 Budget Retreat (Part 3), discussing the 10-year Capital Improvement Program (CIP) model, debt capacity limits, and general fund revenue and expenditure balancing. Council members debated project prioritization frameworks, mayoral budget requests (such as funding for the 2029 World University Games and local economic activation), and options for closing the general fund budget gap without excessive property tax increases. The session served as a strategic working retreat to provide guidance to the city manager for upcoming budget recommendations, with no formal roll-call votes or binding legislative actions taken.

agenda_items.title: Capital Improvement Program (CIP) 10-Year Plan & Process Overview
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented an overview of the 10-year Capital Improvement Program (CIP) budget process, highlighting the receipt of 70 general capital project requests totaling over $200 million for FY27. Council members discussed the need for long-term predictability, realism regarding construction cost overruns, and enhanced transparency for residents.

agenda_items.title: Finance Department & Debt Model Overview
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Finance Director Tim Flora reviewed the city's debt model, fund cash flows, debt portfolio exceeding $1 billion ($614M utilities, $394M governmental), and key financial ratios (debt service as % of operating expense, debt per capita, and adherence to AAA credit rating targets).

agenda_items.title: Strategic Priority Buckets & Prioritization Framework Structure
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council members debated the strategic priority buckets and prioritization framework structure, specifically addressing how to handle multiple overlapping goals, whether to split complex environmental/housing buckets, and how council-submitted initiatives interact with departmental requests.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Consensus reached via sticky-note voting and inclusion of additional categories without formal roll call tally.

agenda_items.title: General Fund Budget Gap Balancing & Revenue Options
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Finance staff presented preliminary general fund budget balancing options, including tax rate allocations (property tax, debt service, solid waste, dedicated housing, transit) and trade-offs between tax increases, employee pay-for-performance/step plans, and minimum livable wage adjustments.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham City Council Budget Retreat: Day 2 - Friday, February 27, 2026 - Part 3
disagreements.issue: Strategic Priority Buckets & Prioritization Framework Structure
disagreements.summary: Debate over whether to consolidate or separate categories in the strategic priority framework and how council member priorities fit alongside departmental submissions.
disagreements.side_a_position: Favorable to more granular category separation and tracking council priorities.
side_a_arguments: Argued for separating out specific categories (like resilience/environmental policies or distinct priority areas) and ensuring council member-specific initiatives and earmarks are clearly evaluated alongside departmental requests.
disagreements.side_b_position: Favorable to streamlined, focused priority buckets.
side_b_arguments: Emphasized that strategy is about choice, too many priorities dilute focus, and the ranking tool / sticky-note exercise provides clear directional signals to staff without needing overly fragmented goal categories.
disagreements.resolution: Council agreed to proceed with the structured priority ranking exercise while allowing individual council members to add specific items/priorities and use stickers for weighted preference signaling.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham City Council Budget Retreat: Day 2 - Friday, February 27, 2026 - Part 3
disagreements.issue: General Fund Budget Gap Balancing: Tax Increases vs. Compensation and Wage Adjustments
disagreements.summary: Discussion and debate over how to close the projected general fund budget gap and whether to raise property taxes or modify step plans, pay-for-performance, and part-time DMLW implementation.

disagreements.side_a_position: Expressed concern over the loss of regional partnership while acknowledging the necessity of moving forward with the project for Durham's water security.
side_a_arguments: Council members and city staff noted that the withdrawal of partner utilities is a loss for regionalism and changes cost recovery timelines down the road, making finished water costs primarily Durham's responsibility.
disagreements.side_b_position: Maintained that despite partner withdrawal, the project remains the best decision for Durham's long-term water needs and operational efficiency.

meetings.title: Durham Joint City County Planning Committee (JCCPC) - February 4, 2026
meetings.executive_summary: At a nearly three-hour JCCPC meeting on February 4, 2026, Chair Nate Baker and members unanimously approved the prior minutes, reviewed 2025 annual reports from the Board of Adjustment, Planning Commission, Durham Open Space and Trails (DOST), and Historic Preservation Commission, and heard an introduction to the unified City-County Open Space Plan targeting 30% land conservation (currently 25.8%). agenda_items.title: Roll Call and Approval of Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Nate Baker called roll with Matt Kopac, Planning Commission Chair Chagaris, and Commissioner Stephen Valentine present at the start (Vice Chair Mike Lee delayed by a two-hour school bus schedule; Wendy Jacobs and Shanetta Burris arriving shortly thereafter; Javiera Caballero absent). agenda_items.title: 2025 Annual Reports: Board of Adjustment and Planning Commission
agenda_items.discussion_summary: BOA Chair Chad Meadows reported 31 cases (+19% YoY) and 25 continuances, flagging increased use of reasonable-accommodation requests as variance workarounds. agenda_items.title: 2025 Annual Reports: DOST and Historic Preservation Commission

Carla Rosenberg and outgoing HPC Chair Alva Horton reported 28 major COAs, St. Joseph's AME/Harriet Tubman YMCA National Register additions, Chicken Hut local landmark status, and frustration over state 365-day demolition-delay limits on Fayetteville Street.

agenda_items.title: Durham City-County Open Space Plan Introduction
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Jay Butts introduced the City-County Open Space Plan with consultant Agency Landscape + Planning and subconsultant Rivington & Reeves, consolidating legacy open space plans and identifying high-conservation parcels for the new LDC Conservation district (10% building coverage, 50% tree coverage) toward the 30% goal (currently 25.8% countywide). Wendy Jacobs stressed clarifying that most of Duke Forest (~5,800 of 7,000 acres) lacks permanent easements and urged exploring green burials and floodplain buyouts.

agenda_items.title: New UDO / LDC Update: Draft Edits, Non-PDR Affordable Proffers, and Adoption Timeline
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Robin Schultz and Sara Young briefed JCCPC on the 630-page LDC draft released January 29—covering SB 382 downzoning protections, consolidated IC districts, a 1975 compact-lot cutoff, RD affordable height bonuses (+2 stories/70 ft), and Lick Creek 20-acre grading limits. agenda_items.discussion_summary: Scott Whiteman and Robin Schultz previewed carryover multi-year projects alongside six new FY27 items: LDC implementation, tree canopy assessment recommendations, Biophilic Cities reporting (per Carl Rist's Council resolution), natural resource overlay research, Urban Design Studios charettes, and Clarity permitting portal deployment. agenda_items.vote_summary: Informational / Formal vote scheduled for April

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham Joint City County Planning Committee (JCCPC) - February 4, 2026
disagreements.issue: Carrying Forward Non-PDR Conditional Development Plans and 79 Proffered Affordable Units Under NCGS 160D-703
disagreements.summary: Members divided over whether to accept losing up to 79 unbuilt affordable units and $102,500 in DHF proffers across seven non-PDR 2015+ rezonings (including 52 units at 3729 Andrew Avenue) to keep the new LDC streamlined and compliant with state conditional-zoning consent laws.
disagreements.side_a_position: Refuse to forfeit 79 legally committed affordable housing units ('79 families') until staff exhausts legacy-chapter or voluntary opt-in options.
side_a_arguments: Nate Baker insisted existing rezoning commitments represent the law of the land and urged exploring whether an isolated legacy appendix or opt-in clause could preserve the 79 units without breaking the LDC's streamlined format.
disagreements.side_b_position: Keep 2015+ PDR districts (~$4M DHF and 2,100-2,200 units) while avoiding a burdensome legacy UDO rewrite that would delay LDC adoption for stagnant projects.
side_b_arguments: Matt Kopac warned that demanding 100% preservation of inactive conditional projects could consume massive staff resources and delay broader affordable-housing gains under the LDC.

County Commissioner Wendy Jacobs opposed creating a massive legacy chapter undercutting years of code simplification, noting six of seven projects lacked site plans, though she urged calling the 3729 Andrew Avenue developer first.
disagreements.resolution: Committee reached conditional consensus directing staff to contact the seven applicants—especially 3729 Andrew Avenue—to seek voluntary opt-in/acknowledgment agreements or confirm abandoned status and report back next month.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham Joint City County Planning Committee (JCCPC) - February 4, 2026
disagreements.issue: Delaying LDC Adoption Timeline (June to August/September) After Consultant Draft Delivery Slip
disagreements.summary: Committee members weighed staff's request to push the joint public hearing from April to August and governing-body adoption from June to September (effective January 1, 2027) after late delivery of the consultant draft compressed Planning Commission review to two weeks.
disagreements.side_a_position: Support extending the joint hearing to August and adoption to September so Planning Commission, residents, and staff can properly review and clean up the 630-page code.
side_a_arguments: Planning Director Sara Young and PC Chair Chagaris warned a two-week turnaround between Feb 24/Mar 10 PC hearings and an April 22 joint hearing risked forcing a rushed 'no' vote or public backlash.

Matt Kopac, Shanetta Burris, County Commissioner Stephen Valentine, and Nate Baker backed giving staff and Planning Commission breathing room while keeping February 24 and March 10 PC meetings on schedule.
disagreements.side_b_position: Warn that further adoption delays carry real consequences by letting incompatible projects submit under the legacy UDO.
side_b_arguments: County Commissioner Wendy Jacobs pushed back initially against a four-month adoption slide, citing proposals like Northgate arriving out of alignment with the Comprehensive Plan during delays, though she ultimately accepted the extension while insisting on holding the August/September commitment firm.
disagreements.resolution: Consensus direction to retain the February 24 and March 10 Planning Commission hearings while initiating August joint public hearing and September adoption scheduling (with an April check-in if consultant turnaround permits earlier review).

meetings.title: Durham City Council Meeting February 2, 2026 (Virtual)
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council held a virtual meeting on February 2, 2026, due to winter weather conditions. The council unanimously voted to refer a controversial contract with Peregrine Technologies for a police operations management platform back to staff. They also approved the manager's priority items, several consent agenda items, appointments to the Durham Performing Arts Center oversight committee, and adopted a substitute motion for the Curly Gardens annexation/utility extension allowing city water service to be extended to the property without full annexation.

agenda_items.title: Opening, Roll Call & Virtual Meeting Housekeeping
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Williams called the virtual meeting to order at 7:00 PM, followed by a moment of silence and the Pledge of Allegiance. City Clerk conducted the roll call, and the Mayor outlined housekeeping rules for the virtual Zoom webinar format.

agenda_items.title: Council Member Announcements & Recognitions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council members shared announcements, recognizing Black History Month, local frontline workers, sanitation crews, and winter storm recovery efforts. Council Member Rist highlighted Transit Equity Day and local tax assistance programs.

agenda_items.title: City Manager's Priority Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Ferguson presented priority items, recommending referring the Peregrine Technologies police operations platform contract back to staff and granting a continuance for the Creek Side mixed-use development zoning map change.

agenda_items.title: Refer Peregrine Technologies Contract Back to Staff
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Council considered the Manager's priority item to refer the controversial Peregrine Technologies contract back to staff without further consideration, following extensive community feedback. Council members expressed support for the manager's recommendation.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed, 7-0 (Motion by Rist, Second by Cabayro, unanimous roll call vote).

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Approval (Items 1, 2, 5, and 9 pulled)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Council reviewed and approved the consent agenda, noting that items 1, 2, 5, and 9 were pulled for separate public comment or discussion.

agenda_items.title: Infrastructure Contracts & Paving Projects Public Hearing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public hearings and presentations were held for capital infrastructure contracts including street repairs, paving, and stormwater projects (Items 4 and 5). Public commenters raised equity concerns regarding capital investments in historically underserved neighborhoods like Hayti compared to gentrifying areas.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation - Curly Gardens & Utility Extension
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public hearing and extensive deliberation on the consolidated annexation for Curly Gardens (Item 17). Property owners and representatives requested water line extension and annexation for 36 multi-family affordable housing units, while community members raised transparency concerns regarding future expansion into Orange County and urban growth boundary (UGB) implications. Ultimately, Council opted for a substitute motion to authorize a utility extension agreement without full annexation.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed substitute motion 6-0 authorizing utility extension agreement without full annexation.

agenda_items.title: DPAC Oversight Committee & Board Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Council voted on board and committee appointments, including the Mayor's Council for Women and the Durham Performing Arts Center (DPAC) Oversight Committee appointments.

votes.item_title: Manager's Priority Item: Refer Peregrine Technologies contract back to staff
votes.notes: Passed unanimously 7-0.
votes.discussion_detail: This manager's priority item involved referring the Peregrine Technologies contract back to staff following public feedback and review. Council members expressed appreciation for the manager's wisdom in referring the item back and for staff listening to council sentiments. Moved by Council Member Wrist and seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Cabayro, the motion passed unanimously 7-0 on a voice vote.

votes.item_title: Substitute Motion for Curly Gardens: Authorize City Manager to enter into utility extension agreement without full annexation
votes.notes: Passed 6-0.
votes.discussion_detail: Council considered an infill project case for Curly Gardens, where Council Member Cook proposed solely extending utilities rather than pursuing full annexation. Council Member Wrist agreed with the approach as a sound infill project with no traffic concerns, while staff provided context on policies and cost-benefit analysis. A substitute motion was framed by the city attorney and planning director to authorize the city manager to enter into a utility extension agreement with the Sidu Living Trust Trustee. Moved by Council Member Cook, the substitute motion passed unanimously 6-0.

votes.item_title: DPAC Oversight Committee Appointments (Rems and James Bullock)
votes.notes: Passed 6-0.
votes.discussion_detail: The mayor brought forward committee appointments for the Durham Performing Arts Center oversight committee. The motion proposed appointing Rems representing arts and culture and James Bullock representing facility management, with terms expiring on March 1st, 2029. Properly moved and seconded, the appointments passed unanimously 6-0.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Work Session 1.22.2026 (Full Audio)
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council held a work session covering winter ice storm preparedness, an unplanned mid-meeting closed session during a livestream audio outage, pulled consent items, and staff presentations on Falls Lake nutrient rules and the Digital Equity Plan. The sharpest debate centered on Agenda Item 10, a proposed $500,000 contract with Peregrine Technologies for a police Real-Time Crime Center data platform, which drew intense public opposition over surveillance and federal data access alongside strong support from residents and Mayor Leonardo Williams seeking tools to combat gun violence. agenda_items.title: Winter Weather and Ice Storm Preparedness Briefing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Bo Ferguson requested taking Presentations 13 and 12 in reverse order and introduced department briefings on an approaching freezing rain and ice storm. Environmental and Street Services Director Marvin Williams outlined salt/sand treatment priorities across 25 outfitted trucks and potential solid waste collection delays, while Deputy City Manager Keith Chadwell covered emergency management activation, off-duty public safety staffing, and mass sheltering plans including limited pet capacity. Community Safety Director Ryan Smith detailed 24/7 shelter expansions for single adults, families, and medically vulnerable residents, HEART street outreach with partner agencies, and triage phone lines.

agenda_items.title: Attorney-Client Consultation Closed Session and Audio Outage Recess
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Attorney Rehberg requested a closed session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) regarding two noticed, unfiled liability claims and potential city participation in an unfiled affirmative litigation action. When a broadcast audio failure required a technical reset at 00:40:55, Mayor Leonardo Williams recessed the open session to conduct the closed session immediately rather than waiting until the end of the meeting. Council reconvened in open session at 2:26 p.m. (01:26:35) once broadcast audio was restored.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Reading (Items 1-11, 14-19) and Public Comments on Council Decorum, COVID Funds, and Traffic Safety
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Leonardo Williams read the upcoming February 2 agenda, noting Items 4, 9, and 10 were pulled for discussion while Item 8 (South Ellerbe Stormwater Project grant) and Public Hearings 14-19 were previewed. During Citizens' Matters, Jacqueline Wagstaff criticized Council decorum at the prior Monday meeting and Victoria Peterson requested an accounting of COVID/ARPA funding and interest earnings. Gregory Williams and grieving father Richard Davis (whose son Isaiah Davis was killed on Guess Road in November 2025) delivered a 300-signature petition urging immediate traffic-calming measures on Guess Road and state-maintained corridors.

agenda_items.title: Contract ST-342: Street Repairs and Repaving 2026 (2024 Bond Referendum)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Nate Baker pulled Item 4 to ask whether bond-funded street repaving incorporates traffic calming and NACTO design standards. Environmental and Street Services manager Clint Blackburn confirmed staff coordinates with Transportation to review all repaving streets against the Bike+Walk Plan, adding restriping, speed cushions, or speed humps where applicable. Baker critiqued auto-centric subdivision design as inducing speeding, while Council Member Carl Rist noted the ongoing joint City-County Bike+Walk Plan update will commit future CIP investments to 25 priority intersections, corridors, off-road links, and gaps.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Settled onto Consent Agenda for Feb 2 meeting

agenda_items.title: Second Amendment to Interlocal Cooperation Agreement with Durham Housing Authority for Security Equipment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Pulled by Council Member Chelsea Cook and resident Victoria Peterson, who asked which public housing sites would receive equipment, this Cycle 3 Participatory Budgeting amendment provides additional contingency funds for cameras, bolt locks, door hardware, and lighting at Preiss-Steele Place and Cornwallis Road. Participatory Budgeting Manager Carmen Ortiz and Durham Housing Authority COO Ashanti Brown explained that delays stemmed from converting to upfront funding and project manager turnover, while cost increases reflected elevator infrastructure and server requirements. Cook questioned ongoing cellular and maintenance costs (which DHA will absorb), and Carl Rist praised the cross-jurisdictional collaboration.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Settled onto Consent Agenda for Feb 2 meeting

agenda_items.title: Contract with Peregrine Technologies, Inc. for DPD Operations Management Platform (Real-Time Crime Center)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Pulled by the public, this proposed ~$500,000 contract drew nine public commenters opposing it over surveillance expansion, predictive policing bias, third-party data aggregation, AI concerns, and potential ICE/federal subpoena exposure, while resident Victoria Peterson urged Council to approve cameras and policing tools to combat shootings in Black neighborhoods. Council Members Chelsea Cook, Nate Baker, Javiera Caballero, and Matt Kopac voiced opposition or serious reservations and called for strict guardrails or a privacy/surveillance commission, while Shanetta Burris and Mayor Leonardo Williams pressed colleagues for concrete solutions to gun violence rather than delaying action. Police Chief Patrice Andrews defended the platform as an investigative tool governed by strict audit policies rather than surveillance.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Moved to General Business Agenda (GBA) for Feb 2 meeting

agenda_items.title: Falls Lake Nutrient Strategy Rules Overview Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Environmental and Street Services staffer Michelle Woolfolk briefed Council on the state's upcoming 2027 rewrite of the 2011 Falls Lake nutrient rules, covering chlorophyll-a standards, strict 0.33 lb/acre/year total phosphorus targets for new development, offset credit scarcity, and the Upper Neuse River Basin Association's (UNRBA) investment-based compliance approach for existing development. Woolfolk warned that an impasse with the state over wastewater discharge caps amid regional growth may prompt UNRBA to petition the Environmental Management Commission with alternate rules as early as April, requiring quick Council action. Council Member Carl Rist highlighted Durham's $160,000 annual UNRBA investment, past wastewater nutrient reductions, and the risk of legislative intervention if 10 or more objections trigger General Assembly review.

agenda_items.title: Digital Equity Plan Update Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Digital Inclusion Program Manager Patrice Carroll and Digital Durham founder Laura Fogle presented progress on Durham's 2021 Digital Equity Plan, noting broadband adoption has reached 94.4% and device access 97% of county households alongside more than 12 new digital skills initiatives. Fogle highlighted Durham's consecutive National Digital Inclusion Association Visionary Trailblazer awards and an ARPA-funded digital navigator program launching February 25 with Durham Literacy Center, Stanford L. Warren Library, Student U, and Families Moving Forward. She flagged AI literacy, cybersecurity, and the end-of-2026 ARPA funding cliff as major upcoming challenges, drawing praise from Mayor Leonardo Williams, Carl Rist, and Chelsea Cook.

side_b_arguments: Residents in high-crime and Black neighborhoods are terrorized by shootings and homicides and deserve tangible tools to help DPD clear cases faster and deliver closure to victims' families.

Repeatedly stalling anti-crime technology proposals with new commissions or task forces without offering viable alternatives fails communities demanding safety.

disagreements.summary: Council members debated whether the proposed density and height bonuses coupled with affordability requirements would effectively incentivize development or if current mechanisms were overly restrictive.
disagreements.side_a_position: Argued that density and height bonuses must be strictly tied to affordable housing requirements to ensure equitable and just growth.
side_a_arguments: Density and height are precious commodities that should not be given away for free without securing meaningful affordable housing units.
Equitable growth around transit corridors requires tying density increases to deep affordability (e.g. 30-60% AMI).

meetings.title: Durham Joint City County Planning Committee (JCCPC) - January 7, 2026

Members then reviewed Comprehensive Plan Policy 103 parkland access criteria and walkshed mapping, debating private-land open space designations, HOA open space exclusion, and whether suburban 10-minute drive metrics dilute walkability goals. The committee also reviewed the full adoption schedule, Module 3 engagement results, and Module 4 administration updates for the new Unified Development Ordinance (renamed the Land Development Code), sparking tension over holding the Planning Commission to a strict March 10 recommendation deadline without continuances.

The committee approved minutes by voice vote with no agenda adjustments or manager priority items. Planning Director Young introduced newly promoted Assistant Director Erlene Thomas, who assumed Bo Derrinsky's portfolio as he transitioned into retired Assistant Director Grace Smith's role.

agenda_items.title: Election of Committee Officers (Chair and Vice Chair)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: JCCPC elected its 2026 leadership by unanimous voice votes.
