agenda_items.title: Access to Parks, Open Space, Trails, and Recreation (Comprehensive Plan Policy 103)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Jay Buds and DPR Senior Planner Austin Bowman presented criteria defining qualifying public parkland, a 'safe 10-minute walk,' and a parkland walkshed map, noting the newer DPR System Plan differentiates urban (10-minute walk), suburban (10-minute drive), and rural (15-minute drive) standards. Committee members raised multiple policy concerns: Chair Jacobs asked about UDO codification, trailhead parking, and linear trails; Matt Kopac asked about overlaying Trust for Public Land demographic equity data; Javiera Caballero opposed designating private land as Open Space on the Place Type Map without funds to buy it at fair market value; Nate Baker questioned exclusionary private HOA open space and relaxing walkability metrics to a 10-minute drive; and Commissioner Valentine asked to exclude lakes/reservoirs from open space land percentages.

agenda_items.title: New Unified Development Ordinance (Land Development Code) Update: Timeline, Engagement, and Administration
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Assistant Director Bo Derrinsky presented the Module 4 Administration section, announced the ordinance's renaming from Unified Development Ordinance (UDO) to Land Development Code (LDC), and outlined the adoption schedule: a special Planning Commission meeting on February 24, a Planning Commission recommendation on March 10, a joint City-County public hearing on April 22, and adoption in May/June 2026. Committee members debated whether the Planning Commission can be held strictly to March 10 without continuances to protect the April 22 joint hearing date. Planner Lisa Miller reported over 1,300 Module 3 survey responses (aided by ~20 engagement ambassadors led by Dr. Allen of TG Allen and Associates, despite zero Spanish-language survey submissions) and detailed public hearing outreach including bilingual signs, library hard copies, and over $120,000 in mailed notices to every property owner and tenant.

votes.notes: Voice vote by JCCPC members present at start of meeting (Nate Baker, Matt Kopac, Commissioners Lee and Valentine, and Planning Commissioner Shagaris; Chair Jacobs arrived later at 00:14:04, and Javiera Caballero participated in the session).

After confirming there were no adjustments to the agenda following roll call, Baker called for a motion to approve the minutes from the prior meeting. An unidentified committee member moved approval and another seconded, with no discussion or objections raised. Baker declared the minutes approved by voice vote.

votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote electing City Council Member Nate Baker as Chair for 2026; Chair Jacobs had not yet arrived.
votes.discussion_detail: Following staff introductions and manager priority checks, the committee moved ahead of schedule to its annual election of officers. Vice Chair Nate Baker explained the standard procedure of electing the Chair first, followed by the Vice Chair. An unidentified committee member moved that Nate Baker serve as Chair of the JCCPC, and another member seconded the motion. No other nominations were offered, and the motion carried unanimously by voice vote with no recorded opposition.

votes.item_title: Election of County Commissioner Lee as JCCPC Vice Chair
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote electing County Commissioner Dr. Lee as Vice Chair after clarifying the committee's informal City-County rotation practice.

Because Baker represents the City, members agreed the Vice Chair seat should rotate to a County representative. A committee member then moved to elect County Commissioner Dr. Lee as Vice Chair, which was seconded and passed unanimously by voice vote.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham Joint City County Planning Committee (JCCPC) - January 7, 2026
disagreements.issue: Parkland Access Standards (10-Minute Walk vs. Suburban Drive) and Private Open Space Designations
disagreements.summary: Committee members debated staff proposals to align the Comprehensive Plan's 10-minute walk parkland target with the DPR System Plan's 10-minute suburban drive standard, as well as the fairness and enforceability of designating private parcels as open space without municipal acquisition funds.
disagreements.side_a_position: Preserve strict walkability metrics and protect private property owners from uncompensated open space designations by pairing Place Type designations with funded acquisition.
side_a_arguments: Redefining suburban success around a 10-minute drive lowers the bar for walkable, mixed-use, connected growth, especially when even a 10-minute walk is double the traditional 5-minute walkshed standard.
Private HOA open space can be exclusionary and inaccessible to the general public unless public access easements and public-park design standards are required.
Designating 75% of a private owner's parcel as Recreation/Open Space on the Place Type Map without government funds to purchase it at fair market value is unfair and invites legal challenges.
disagreements.side_b_position: Adopt tiered urban/suburban/rural access benchmarks as realistic short-term operational standards and use Place Type open space designations to reflect floodway and natural heritage constraints.
side_b_arguments: Achieving a 10-minute walk for every resident within a 10-year planning horizon is operationally and fiscally unrealistic without massive land acquisition and sidewalk infrastructure outside the urban core.
Suburban 10-minute drive and rural 15-minute drive tiers act as incremental benchmarks toward long-term urbanization while acknowledging destinations like Eno River State Park.

Open space designations on private land mostly reflect undevelopable floodways, floodplains, and natural heritage areas, and zoning still allows reasonable private development while the upcoming Open Space Plan identifies acquisition priorities.
side_b_members: Planning Staff (Austin Bowman, Jay Buds, Scott)
disagreements.resolution: Informational item; staff agreed to return with an updated walkshed map incorporating county/state/NGO parkland, density-to-walkshed examples, and a fiscal acquisition analysis under the upcoming Open Space Plan.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham Joint City County Planning Committee (JCCPC) - January 7, 2026
disagreements.issue: Enforcing a Strict March 10 Planning Commission Deadline Without Continuances for the New Land Development Code (UDO)
disagreements.summary: Elected officials and Planning Commission representatives clashed over holding the Planning Commission to a firm two-meeting schedule (February 24 and March 10) with no continuances so the joint City-County public hearing can proceed on April 22 and final adoption can occur in May/June 2026.
disagreements.side_a_position: Hold the Planning Commission strictly to the March 10 recommendation deadline with no continuances to prevent delays to the April 22 joint public hearing and June 2026 adoption.
side_a_arguments: Providing two Planning Commission meetings (February 24 and March 10) instead of an expedited single hearing was already the December JCCPC compromise.
Coordinating a joint public hearing between the City Council and Board of County Commissioners (scheduled April 22) is logistically difficult and cannot be pushed back.
Opponents who dislike the already-adopted Comprehensive Plan should not be allowed to manipulate the UDO/LDC implementation process through repeated continuances after seven years of work.
disagreements.side_b_position: Ensure the volunteer Planning Commission has sufficient time and respect to review the massive document thoroughly, resolve questions, and incorporate public input rather than being rushed or bypassed.
side_b_arguments: The Planning Commission is the primary venue where residents feel heard before elected boards make final policy decisions, and volunteer commissioners should not be disrespected or bypassed.

Given the short two-week window between February 24 and March 10 and statutory notice rules, it is challenging to resolve all technical questions on a multi-hundred-page code unless commissioners receive full materials and answers well in advance.
disagreements.resolution: Committee consensus formed around sending full LDC materials to Planning Commissioners immediately after the January Council work session, scheduling small-group staff briefings (under quorum limits) to resolve questions early, and encouraging the Planning Commission to issue its recommendation with attached suggested edits on March 10 (with Nate Baker and Bo Derrinsky supporting that approach).

meetings.title: Durham City Council January 5, 2026
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council held its first meeting of 2026 on January 5, 2026. The council proclaimed Human Trafficking Prevention Month and celebrated the 25th anniversary of Together for Resilient Youth (TRI). Following a public hearing with extensive public comment on the Sage Brook townhouses annexation and rezoning project, the council debated infrastructure capacity, traffic, environmental buffers, and comprehensive plan alignment. Ultimately, the council approved the annexation and utility extension agreement, the zoning map amendment (both 4-3), and the consistency statement (7-0).

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, Pledge of Allegiance, and Roll Call
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Leonardo Williams called the meeting to order, mentioning a 'mayor for a day' guest with a rare disease. Council held a moment of silence and recited the Pledge of Allegiance, followed by a roll call confirming all council members present.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation: Human Trafficking Prevention Month
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tempore Javier Cavierro read a proclamation recognizing January 2026 as Human Trafficking Prevention Month, accompanied by survivor advocate Reverend Cara Matthews from Shield NC who discussed grooming and myths surrounding human trafficking.

agenda_items.title: Announcements by Council Members
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council members shared brief New Year remarks, reflecting on family milestones, upcoming budget priorities, affordable housing challenges, and concerns regarding recent spikes in gun violence.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation: 25th Anniversary of Together for Resilient Youth (TRI)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Leonardo Williams presented a proclamation recognizing the 25th anniversary of Together for Resilient Youth (TRI) to Dr. Wanda Boon, highlighting their public health model, overdose prevention work, and community resilience efforts.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Sage Brook Townhouses Annexation and Rezoning
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public hearing regarding the Annexation Ordinance, Zoning Map Amendment (from Rural/Suburban to Planned Development Residential), and Consistency Statement for Sage Brook Townhouses. Several residents spoke on traffic impacts, lack of EMS and medical infrastructure, stream buffers, and agricultural concerns, while the applicant's attorney responded regarding site design, impervious surfaces, and utility connectivity.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed across three separate votes (Annexation 4-3, Rezoning 4-3, Consistency Statement 7-0)

votes.item_title: Annexation Ordinance and Utility Extension Agreement for Sage Brook Townhouses
votes.notes: Motion to adopt an ordinance annexing Sage Brook townhouses into the city of Durham and authorizing the city manager to enter into a utility extension agreement with Capital City Homes LLC.
votes.discussion_detail: The Durham City Council considered an annexation ordinance and utility extension agreement for the Sage Brook Townhouses project with Capital City Homes LLC. The discussion touched upon broader themes of housing affordability for younger residents in Durham, housing abundance frameworks, and regional growth challenges. Council members debated the impacts of development, with specific mentions of traffic, local infrastructure, and farmland preservation in Southeast Durham leading to a commitment to review local growth patterns. The motion ultimately passed by a 4-3 vote, with Council Members Baker, Burrus, and Cook voting in opposition.

votes.item_title: Zoning Map Amendment for Sage Brook Townhouses
votes.notes: Ordinance amending the UDO from Residential Rural (RR) / Jordan Watershed Overlay District B County to Planned Development Residential 6.9 (PDR-6.9) / Jordan Watershed Overlay District B City jurisdiction.
votes.discussion_detail: The council voted on a zoning map amendment for the Sage Brook Townhouses project to amend the unified development ordinance by taking property out of the county's residential suburban 20 Jordan Watershed Overlay District B jurisdiction and establishing it as planned development residential 6.905 within the city's jurisdiction. This zoning change supported the high-density residential townhouse development proposed by Capital City Homes LLC. The motion passed 4 to 3, with Council Members Baker, Burrus, and Cook casting the dissenting votes.

votes.item_title: Consistency Statement for Sage Brook Townhouses
votes.notes: Required consistency statement pursuant to NC General Statutes Section 160D-605.
votes.discussion_detail: The council considered adopting the required statutory consistency statement under North Carolina General Statutes Section 160D-605 regarding the Sage Brook Townhouses zoning amendment and development plans. Unlike the contentious votes on the annexation and zoning map amendments, the consistency statement motion was adopted unanimously with a 7-0 vote.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham City Council January 5, 2026
disagreements.issue: Sage Brook Townhouses Annexation and Rezoning (Non-Contiguous Development, Infrastructure, and Environmental Impact)
disagreements.summary: Debate over whether to approve the non-contiguous Sage Brook townhouses annexation and rezoning project, balancing housing need and tax base expansion against infrastructure strain and rural transition concerns.

City Attorney reported no priority items. The Board and Committee report confirmed advisory board and commission appointments including Durham Cultural Advisory Board and Human Relations Commission.

agenda_items.title: Citizen Matters / Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public comments were delivered by multiple residents addressing free speech, council decorum, community activism, and recent actions regarding public access and civic participation at City Hall.

agenda_items.title: Update on Forever Home Durham
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented an update on the Forever Home Durham initiative, reviewing progress on creating and preserving affordable rental units, low-income household stabilization, and minority/women-owned business enterprise (MWBE) contracting goals. Council members discussed down payment assistance loan numbers, the eviction diversion program, affordability periods, and long-term housing levers.

agenda_items.title: Parking Program Overview
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented an overview of the downtown parking program, discussing parking utilization, deck vacancy, downtown worker discount programs, surface parking lots, and potential strategies like one-hour free parking and pricing adjustments to manage curb space demand.

agenda_items.title: Approval of the Settlement of the Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The city manager reviewed the settled agenda items including consent items 1-10 and GBA public hearing items 13 and 14 (with items 3, 4, and 5 pulled by Council Member Cook). A motion was made, seconded, and unanimously approved to settle the agenda.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed, Unanimous (Moved and properly seconded, all in favor)

meetings.title: Durham City Council December 15, 2025
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council met on December 15, 2025, presided over by Mayor Leonardo Williams. The council adopted the Downtown Durham Blueprint 2035 Plan amending the Comprehensive Plan, approved zoning map changes and annexation for the Page Road Amendment (up to 15 townhomes), unanimously failed a non-contiguous conservation subdivision annexation/rezoning for Hamlin Reserve (2503 & 2523 Hamlin Road), and held a contentious public hearing on the 81.75-acre Lee Village Center compact suburban design rezoning (Z-23-00042), ultimately voting 6-1 to continue the public hearing and case to February 16, 2026.

agenda_items.title: Opening, Roll Call, and Meeting Protocol
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The meeting opened with a moment of silence, the Pledge of Allegiance, and a roll call. Mayor Leonardo Williams read a formal statement regarding decorum in council chambers and adherence to North Carolina General Statute 143-318.17 concerning meeting disruptions and removal procedures.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Proclamations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The council presented two ceremonial proclamations: one recognizing the Salvation Army of Durham Holiday Impact Recognition Day (accepted by Major Angela and David Rivas), and another celebrating the 90th anniversary of the Durham Committee on Affairs of Black People (accepted by Senator Floyd McKissick and committee representatives).

agenda_items.title: Announcements by City Council
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council members shared announcements, congratulating community organizations, addressing recent tragic shootings globally and locally (including support for injured Durham Academy graduate Kendall Turner), highlighting white flag shelter bed expansions and homeless support services, and discussing community events.

agenda_items.title: CAPER Public Hearing & Housing Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City staff presented the Consolidated Annual Performance and Evaluation Report (CAPER) detailing HUD formula block grant funding (CDBG, HOME, HOPWA, ESG) and program achievements. Public commenters and council members discussed housing expenditures, unspent allocations, and homelessness supportive services.

agenda_items.title: Downtown Durham Blueprint 2035 Plan Comprehensive Plan Amendment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Downtown Durham Incorporated (DDI) presented the Downtown Durham Blueprint 2035 plan, establishing a shared vision and targeted goals for downtown vibrancy, infrastructure, and growth. Following public comments, the council approved the comprehensive plan amendment.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed unanimously (7-0), moved by Council, seconded, vote closed at [01:30:59].

agenda_items.title: Page Road Amendment Zoning Map Change & Consistency Statement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The council considered a zoning map change for 3404 Page Road (Z-25-00010) to amend the development plan across three parcels. Staff presented the application, the council held a public hearing, and subsequently approved the map change and consistency statement.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed unanimously (7-0); map change vote at [01:35:25], consistency statement vote at [01:35:45].

agenda_items.title: 3306 Page Road Annexation & Utility Extension Agreement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The council reviewed a request for utility extension and annexation for 3306 Page Road to allow up to 15 townhouse units. Discussion covered utility agreements, connection terms, and monetary contributions before approval.

agenda_items.title: Hamlin Reserve Annexation & Rezoning
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The council reviewed the annexation and rezoning petition for Hamlin Reserve (2503 & 2523 Hamlin Road) involving 42.61 acres for a conservation subdivision. Council members debated consistency with the urban growth boundary and environmental considerations before voting against the annexation.

agenda_items.title: Lee Village Center Rezoning & Annexation (Z-23-00042) Continuance
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The council held a lengthy public hearing and deliberation on the Lee Village Center rezoning and annexation (Z-23-00042). Substantive debate centered around Traffic Impact Analysis (TIA) requirements and timing, transit-oriented development connectivity, and future bus stop placement, culminating in a motion to continue the case.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed (6-1, with Council Member Cook voting no), vote closed at [03:53:28] / [03:53:28] transcript timeline (~05:35:28).

votes.item_title: Downtown Durham Blueprint 2035 Plan Comprehensive Plan Amendment
votes.discussion_detail: Downtown Durham Incorporated President and CEO Nicole Thompson presented the Downtown Durham Blueprint 2035 plan to the City Council, requesting its adoption as an official city plan following a two-year engagement process involving over 2,300 people. The blueprint features a shared vision, seven targeted goals with deliberate strategies, and implementable actions to support continued growth and vibrancy while preserving downtown's unique character. Following a public hearing with one public speaker, the council entertained a motion to adopt a resolution amending the Durham Comprehensive Plan, which passed unanimously with a 7-0 vote.

votes.item_title: Page Road Amendment Zoning Map Change (3404 Page Road / Z-25-00010)
votes.discussion_detail: Pamela Porter of TMTLA Associates proposed amending an existing graphic development plan (Z-17-00031) on three parcels located at 0, 1000, and 1002 Oak Mill Drive to allow an additional external access point on the eastern portion adjacent to 3306 Page Road. The current Planned Development Residential 5.788 zoning designation remained unchanged, and the amendment was graphically depicted on sheet three of attachment D. Staff and applicant presented the request during a public hearing, after which the council voted to adopt the ordinance and consistency statement, passing both unanimously with a 7-0 vote.

votes.item_title: Page Road Amendment Consistency Statement
votes.discussion_detail: Following the zoning map change presentation and public hearing for the 3404 Page Road amendment, the council considered adopting a consistency statement as required by North Carolina General Statute Section 160D-605. The motion was properly moved and seconded, and the clerk opened the vote. The consistency statement passed unanimously with a 7-0 vote.

votes.item_title: 3306 Page Road Annexation & Utility Extension Agreement
votes.discussion_detail: Pamela Porter of TMTLA Associates and Jeff Palmer of Shenandoah Homes requested a utility extension agreement, voluntary annexation, and initial zoning map change for a 1.82-acre parcel at 3306 Page Road from Residential Rural to Planned Development Residential 8.876 to allow up to 15 townhouse units as a contiguous expansion of the Page Oaks neighborhood. The applicant addressed council questions regarding pedestrian and cyclist access, confirming a commitment to build a 10-foot shared path connecting the terminus of Oak Mill Drive to the path on Page Road without vehicular connection. After addressing a brief procedural mix-up in motion ordering, the council adopted the annexation ordinance, utility extension agreement, and required consistency statement, all passing unanimously with a 7-0 vote.

votes.item_title: Hamlin Reserve Annexation & Rezoning (2503 & 2523 Hamlin Road)
votes.discussion_detail: The council considered an annexation and rezoning request for Hamlin Reserve (2503 and 2523 Hamlin Road). Extensive discussion focused on whether approving the conservation-subdivision model outside the urban growth boundary would set a problematic precedent for future developments and undermine growth boundary enforcement, with council members drawing comparisons to the unanimously rejected Mariah Ridge case. Concerns were also raised regarding the developer, KB Homes, and their alleged inaction regarding ruined wells down on Junction Road. Citing consistency and the importance of adhering to the urban growth boundary, all council members voted against the motion. The motion failed unanimously with a 0-7 vote, with Nays recorded from Mayor Williams, Mayor Pro Tem Caballero, and Council Members Baker, Burris, Cook, Copack, and Rist.

votes.item_title: Lee Village Center Rezoning & Annexation (Z-23-00042) Continuance
votes.discussion_detail: The council considered a motion to keep the public hearing open and continue the rezoning and annexation case for the Lee Village Center (Z-23-00042) until February 16, 2026. Discussion centered around outstanding questions regarding traffic impact analyses (TIA), parkland priorities, mix of uses, and neighborhood street connectivity. Members noted that transit infrastructure like bus shelters, pads, and pullouts would be implemented at the site plan phase per compact urban design standards and zoning commitments. Despite resident opposition regarding connectivity and concerns about the application's details, several members expressed willingness to grant a continuance to give the new council time to address questions. The motion passed 6-1, with Council Member Cook voting in opposition.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham City Council December 15, 2025
disagreements.issue: Traffic Impact Analysis (TIA) requirement and timing for large rezoning (Lee Village Center, Z-23-00042)
disagreements.summary: Debate over whether a Traffic Impact Analysis (TIA) was legally mandated prior to zoning approval for the 81.75-acre Lee Village Center project, or whether deferring granular TIAs to the site plan stage was appropriate.
disagreements.side_a_position: Require TIA immediately or send back to planning department; oppose voting/continuing without strict statutory compliance.
side_a_arguments: A TIA is strictly required by UDO section 3.3 at the time of zoning change (word 'shall' is mandatory); voting without it is a dereliction of duty.
disagreements.side_b_position: Accept planning director's determination; perform granular TIAs at each phase of site plan approval while continuing the public hearing to Feb 16, 2026 to resolve park and use clarity.
side_b_arguments: Under 160D-405, administrative appeal window on planning director's TIA decision has passed; due to large phased buildout (1,667–2,294 units over 10-20 years) and form-based compact suburban design, scoping an overall TIA violates rational nexus/rough proportionality, making site-plan level TIAs more rigorous and appropriate.
side_b_members: Applicant legal counsel, Planning Director, Mayor Williams, and majority of Council
disagreements.resolution: Motion to continue the public hearing and case to February 16, 2026 passed 6-1 (Council Member Cook voted against continuing/passing because she argued a TIA is legally mandated prior to zoning approval).

meetings.title: Durham City Council Work Session December 4, 2025
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council convened for a Work Session on December 4, 2025, presided over by Mayor Williams. The council discussed administrative consent items, heard presentations on the 505 West Chapel Hill Street redevelopment options (including preservation via Preservation North Carolina), reviewed the 2025 third quarter crime report, and examined the FY 2025-2026 first quarter financial report. Several consent items were pulled for separate discussion, and Item 10 (redevelopment loan agreement with Durham Housing Authority) was referred back to staff upon request.

agenda_items.title: Council Announcements, Roll Call, and Meeting Decorum
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Williams called the meeting to order and roll call was conducted. Council members shared announcements including participatory budgeting updates, the Carolina Theater centennial campaign, and local sports events. Mayor Williams addressed decorum following disruptions at a prior meeting and announced new time limits for council member discussions.

agenda_items.title: City Manager & City Attorney Priority Updates
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager announced winter weather monitoring, introduced Starleta Tanner as the new permanent director of Community Partnerships and Engagement, and noted that DHA requested item 10 be referred back to staff. The City Attorney requested a closed session for attorney-client consultation on as-yet-unfiled litigation.

agenda_items.title: Board and Committee Appointments Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Clerk presented board and committee appointments, including Frederica Cadeno for the Participatory Budgeting Steering Committee (youth category) and Doug Pender for the Durham Convention and Visitors Bureau Discover Durham appointment.

agenda_items.title: Public Comments: Swing Pals Program
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Doug Hodges, founder and executive director of Swing Pals, spoke during Citizens Matter about the nonprofit providing mindfulness and golf resilience coaching for underserved youth in Durham public schools and thanked the council for supporting Hillendale Golf Course.

agenda_items.title: Hiring Practices Performance Audit (November 2025)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Audit Services Director Germaine presented a performance audit on hiring practices, discussing timelines, application processes, and recommendations to streamline hiring. HR manager Jim O'Donnell answered questions regarding applicant onboarding and job application requirements.

agenda_items.title: Tennis Court Lighting Purchase Contracts (Whipperwill Park & Rock Quarry Park)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council discussed purchase contracts for tennis court lighting at Whipperwill Park and Rock Quarry Park with Musco Sports Lighting LLC, focusing on Dark Sky compliance, lighting fixtures, spillover reduction, and fixture design standards.

agenda_items.title: Proposed Lease with Durham Regional Association of Realtors at 4238 University Drive
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council discussed a proposed lease agreement with the Durham Regional Association of Realtors Incorporated at 4238 University Drive, reviewing lease terms, property usage, and real estate department details.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Annexation: Lee Village Center
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council reviewed the consolidated annexation for Lee Village Center (and related zoning/development items), discussing traffic impact analysis (TIA) requirements, UDO compliance, density thresholds, and planning commission recommendations.

agenda_items.title: Update on Redevelopment of 505 West Chapel Hill Street
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Extensive presentation and deliberation on redevelopment scenarios for the 505 West Chapel Hill Street site (Home Security Life Insurance Building). Topics included building preservation vs. demolition, estimated rehab costs ($25-30M), historic preservation covenants with Preservation North Carolina, interim activation open space, and affordable housing financing constraints (9% LIITC and parking requirements).

agenda_items.title: 2025 Third Quarter Crime Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Durham Police Department presented the 2025 third quarter crime report, reviewing violent crime trends through September, homicides (36 to date), domestic incidents, robberies, firearm involvement, and aggravated assaults.

agenda_items.title: Fiscal Year 2025-2026 First Quarter Financial Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented the FY 2025-2026 first quarter financial report, discussing quarterly stoplight reports, budget performance, CIP reporting, and departmental financial tracking.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session: Attorney-Client Consultation on As-Yet-Unfiled Litigation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Pursuant to NC General Statute 143-318.11(a)(3), the city attorney requested and council voted to enter closed session for attorney-client consultation to discuss as-yet-unfiled litigation.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Approved unanimously (Motion by Council Member Cook)

meetings.title: Durham Joint City County Planning Committee (JCCPC) December 3, 2025
meetings.executive_summary: The Joint City-County Planning Committee (JCCPC) reviewed consolidated monthly development case summaries across the Urban Growth Boundary and held extensive work-session policy discussions on the draft New Unified Development Ordinance (UDO). Committee members debated the acreage threshold for Planned Development Districts, the sunset date for pre-2015 approved development plans, sidewalk requirements outside the Urban Growth Boundary, and the pace of the UDO adoption schedule versus Planning Commission review capacity. No substantive UDO policies came to a formal vote; the committee took two procedural voice votes approving the November 5, 2025 minutes and excusing absences including Council Member Matt Kopac.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Agenda Adjustments, and RTP 3.0 Announcement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Jacobs opened the meeting while awaiting a quorum, which arrived at 00:05:42 with Vice Chair Nate Baker, Planning Commissioner Shagaris, and Commissioner Burton present (Javiera Caballero joined later at 00:29:42). Chair Jacobs announced that the Durham County Board of Commissioners had approved the RTP 3.0 rezoning prior to Thanksgiving following the county's earlier $20 million hub investment.

agenda_items.title: Approval of November 5, 2025 Meeting Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Once quorum was confirmed following roll call, the committee considered the November 5, 2025 JCCPC meeting minutes. Vice Chair Nate Baker moved approval and Commissioner Burton seconded with no edits requested.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated Case Summaries
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented eight active zoning map change applications, predominantly small townhouse and multifamily residential projects inside the Urban Growth Boundary. Vice Chair Nate Baker highlighted positively that recent submittals have shifted away from large suburban subdivisions toward smaller infill projects within existing growth boundaries.

agenda_items.title: New UDO: Planned Development Districts and Pre-2015 Development Plan Sunsets
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff briefed JCCPC on mapping rules for existing approved development plans—proposing to revert pre-2015 unbuilt projects to standard UDO base districts—and proposed a 150-acre minimum threshold for Planned Development (PD) districts. Nate Baker urged lowering the PD minimum to 50–80 acres to allow coordinated master-planned infill, whereas Javiera Caballero cautioned that smaller PD sites struggle to finance public benefits such as schools and parks, and Chair Jacobs floated a compromise around 100 acres.

agenda_items.title: Excused Absences for Commissioners Lee, Valentine, and Council Member Matt Kopac
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After Javiera Caballero arrived and joined the committee, members formally voted to excuse the absences of Commissioner Lee, Commissioner Valentine, and Council Member Matt Kopac.

agenda_items.title: New UDO Review Timeline, Planning Commission Schedule, and County Sidewalks
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Members clashed over whether to expedite UDO adoption or preserve multi-meeting Planning Commission review, sparked by Javiera Caballero's critique of community engagement around the Northgate Mall site and Nate Baker's defense of deliberative Planning Commission review amid state downzoning restrictions. Staff also sought direction on sidewalk construction rules outside the Urban Growth Boundary—whether to build along frontage, require off-site extensions within a quarter-mile, or mandate sidewalk completion along adopted Bike+Walk and rail trail plans.

votes.item_title: Approval of November 5, 2025 JCCPC Meeting Minutes
votes.notes: Javiera Caballero arrived later at 00:29:42; Matt Kopac, Commissioner Lee, and Commissioner Valentine were absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Chair Jacobs initially held off on calling the minutes vote at 00:04:12 until enough city and county appointees arrived to establish a quorum. Once Commissioner Burton entered the room at 00:05:42 and the clerk confirmed roll call with Chair Jacobs, Vice Chair Nate Baker, Planning Commissioner Shagaris, and Commissioner Burton present, Chair Jacobs called up approval of the November 5, 2025 minutes. Nate Baker moved to approve the minutes and Commissioner Burton seconded the motion without objection or requested corrections. The motion carried unanimously by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Approval of Excused Absences for Commissioners Lee, Valentine, and Council Member Matt Kopac
votes.notes: Vote occurred following Javiera Caballero's arrival at 00:29:42.
votes.discussion_detail: Following Javiera Caballero's arrival during the New UDO presentation, Vice Chair Nate Baker requested a formal vote to record excused absences for absent committee members before continuing the technical UDO discussion. Committee members noted absences for county appointees Lee and Valentine alongside city appointee Matt Kopac, who was joining the seated council cohort starting in December 2025. Nate Baker moved to approve the excused absences and Javiera Caballero seconded. The committee approved the motion unanimously by voice vote.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham Joint City County Planning Committee (JCCPC) December 3, 2025
disagreements.issue: New UDO Minimum Acreage Threshold for Planned Development Districts
disagreements.summary: Committee members disagreed on staff's proposed 150-acre minimum site size to qualify for a Planned Development (PD) zoning district.
disagreements.side_a_position: Lower the Planned Development threshold to 50–80 acres to encourage cohesive master-planned infill inside the Urban Growth Boundary.
side_a_arguments: Few contiguous parcels inside the Urban Growth Boundary reach 150 acres, so a high floor effectively restricts Planned Developments to greenfield sprawl.
Medium-scale 50–80 acre sites can coordinate streets, parks, and mixed uses without relying on ad-hoc rezonings.
disagreements.side_b_position: Maintain a higher threshold (~100–150 acres) so Planned Development entitlements are tied to major infrastructure and community benefits.
side_b_arguments: Smaller projects rarely have the financial capacity to deliver schools, regional parks, or transformative community benefits.
A ~100-acre compromise avoids opening PD flexibility to mid-sized sites lacking meaningful public-benefit leverage.
disagreements.resolution: Staff agreed to study a smaller PD threshold option and return with refined analysis in January 2026.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham Joint City County Planning Committee (JCCPC) December 3, 2025
disagreements.issue: Pace of New UDO Adoption Timeline vs. Planning Commission Review Depth
disagreements.summary: Javiera Caballero and Nate Baker clashed sharply over community engagement effectiveness (citing Northgate Mall) and whether the New UDO schedule should be accelerated or preserve multi-meeting Planning Commission review.
disagreements.side_a_position: Expedite New UDO adoption and tighten Planning Commission review timelines while reassessing traditional engagement channels.
side_a_arguments: Community engagement around Northgate Mall produced confusion and failed to reflect neighborhood priorities compared to Braggtown outreach.
Delaying UDO adoption slows implementation of Comprehensive Plan housing and equitable growth policies.
disagreements.side_b_position: Preserve thorough Planning Commission deliberation across multiple meetings rather than rushing the UDO rewrite.
side_b_arguments: Planning Commissioners cannot responsibly digest a massive new development code and zoning map in a single rushed session.
North Carolina state restrictions on downzoning make getting the initial UDO mapping right even more consequential.
disagreements.resolution: Staff committed to returning in January 2026 with a revised schedule allocating two earlier Planning Commission meetings ahead of governing-body public hearings.

meetings.title: Durham City Council December 1, 2025
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham City Council held its organizational and regular meeting on December 1, 2025, celebrating outgoing council members and swearing in newly elected officials including Mayor Leonardo Williams, Council Members Matt Copac, Shannetta Burus, and Chelsea Cook. The council discussed community mutual aid and relief efforts responding to recent ICE and Border Patrol immigration enforcement actions across the region. Additionally, the council voted unanimously to adopt a zoning map amendment / UDO change for a residential planned development along with its required statutory consistency statement.

agenda_items.title: Organizational Meeting & Presentation of Certificates of Election
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Durham County Board of Elections presented ceremonial certificates of election to newly elected municipal officials, including Mayor Leonardo Williams, Ward 1 Councilmember Matt Kopac, Ward 2 Councilmember Shannetta Burus, and Ward 3 Councilmember Chelsea Cook, following the 2025 municipal elections.

agenda_items.title: Farewell Remarks and Service Recognitions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The council honored outgoing council members, particularly Ward 1 Councilmember Dedrianna Freeman, for their years of service and dedication to the city, sharing reflections on community advocacy and institutional legacy.

agenda_items.title: Election of Mayor Pro Tempore
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The council considered the appointment of a new Mayor Pro Tempore, culminating in the nomination and unanimous appointment of Councilmember Javier Caviierro as the city's new Mayor Pro Tempore, followed by the oath of office.

agenda_items.title: Council Member Announcements & Community Updates
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council members shared updates on community responses to recent ICE enforcement raids in the Triangle, mutual aid and food distribution efforts by the Durham Community Care Collective, World AIDS Day, and Jordan High School's theatrical partnership with Broadway.

agenda_items.title: Discussion on Municipal Election Schedule and Costs
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Williams raised questions regarding the high cost of odd-year municipal elections and requested an analysis from the Board of Elections regarding potential shifts to even-year elections or four-year mayoral terms to evaluate turnout and fiscal impacts.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing and Zoning Map Amendment for Planned Development Residential
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The council held a public hearing on a request to amend the unified development ordinance (UDO) and rezone 3.35 acres on East Geer Street from Residential Suburban-20 to Planned Development Residential (PDR) for a 22-townhome infill development. Attorney Neil Gos presented developer commitments including environmental buffers, multi-use paths, and housing fund contributions.

votes.item_title: UDO Amendment / Zoning Map Change for Planned Development Residential
votes.discussion_detail: The Durham City Council considered an ordinance to amend the unified development ordinance by taking property out of residential suburban 20 (with Falls/Jordan watershed overlay district B and major transportation corridor I-85) and establishing it as planned development residential. Council members discussed questions regarding project boundary buffers, open space requirements, and minimizing impacts on wetlands and environmentally sensitive areas. Applicant and staff addressed follow-on questions from the planning commission, offering additional commitments on open space location and buffers not strictly required under the comprehensive plan. The motion to adopt the zoning amendment passed unanimously (7-0).

votes.item_title: NCGS 160D-605 Consistency Statement for Zoning Amendment
votes.discussion_detail: Following the approval of the zoning map change for the planned development residential project, the Council considered the statutory consistency statement required by North Carolina General Statute section 160D-605. A motion to adopt the consistency statement was duly moved and seconded. The vote was opened, closed, and passed unanimously (7-0).
